news.Title: Marvell Stock Is Bouncing Back. 3 Reasons the Bulls Aren’t Backing Down.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock has started recovering after it got caught up in the recent AI selloff. After spending most of last week in the red, shares have been climbing this week. Including this morning gains, MRVL stock is up about 6% for the week, joining a broader rebound in semiconductor stocks after a tough period for the sector.

At its Oct. 6 Investor Day, the chipmaker raised its revenue goals and shared plans to become a bigger supplier of AI infrastructure. Marvell's custom AI chips, data center connectivity business, and improving growth outlook are three reasons why analysts believe this rebound has staying power.

More News from Barchart

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 20

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Charlie Munger Said He Was Still Buying Apartment Complexes 'To Give Me Something To Do' but Ran Them the Opposite Way, 'It's All Deferred Gratification'

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

1. Marvell's Custom AI Chips Could Become a Much Bigger Business

The AI chip race is moving beyond standard GPUs. Big cloud companies are now creating processors that fit their specific needs, aiming for better performance, lower power use, and reduced costs. Marvell makes custom chips for these companies, so it stands to gain as more data centers use proprietary AI processors.

At its Investor Day, management raised its custom-chip revenue target for fiscal 2029 to more than $12 billion, up from the previous goal of more than $10 billion. The company now expects custom revenue to more than triple by 2029, thanks to anticipated growth in programs for large cloud customers. Although these are just goals for now, this upgraded outlook shows just how confident management feels about the business. Marvell's expanded Google partnership is another reason to be bullish. If Marvell reaches certain milestones, its expanded partnership with Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google could bring in as much as $120 billion in sales by fiscal 2033. This suggests Marvell's custom-chip business is becoming more important as cloud providers seek processors built for their needs.

2. Connectivity Is Emerging as a Second Major Growth Engine

AI requires more than computing power, and it is becoming a new growth area for Marvell. Large AI clusters rely on fast connections between chips, servers, and racks, which increases the need for optical interconnects, digital signal processors, and networking technology. Marvell provides solutions across these areas and supports the wider AI infrastructure, not just processors.

Story Continues

In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Marvell made $2.17 billion from data center revenue. This was a 46% increase from the year-ago quarter and made up 79% of the company's total sales. During the investor day event, management also attributed the fiscal 2028 revenue target to connectivity. This indicates that the company's higher expectations are not based solely on one custom-chip opportunity. Management also highlighted opportunities in faster optical networking, including 1.6-terabit and future 3.2-terabit technologies, as AI data centers require increasingly high-speed connections.

3. Wall Street Has a Much Bigger Growth Story to Consider

Also at its Investor Day, Marvell made a bold move by raising its long-term targets. The company now aims for revenue between $70 billion and $90 billion, with $80 billion as the midpoint. For comparison, Marvell's fiscal 2026 revenue was $8.2 billion. To hit the midpoint, Marvell would need to grow its annual revenue to nearly ten times its 2026 level within just five years. Management now estimates that its total addressable market could reach about $400 billion by 2030, four times its earlier estimate. This shows why management believes the company can grow significantly without relying on just one new product or customer.

The company is focused on more than just revenue growth. For fiscal 2031, Marvell aims for gross margins between 56% and 59%, operating margins of 44% to 46%, free cash flow margins above 36%, and adjusted EPS over $30 at the midpoint of its revenue forecast. Management said these targets reflect current customer relationships, recent design wins, ongoing development programs, and plans to secure supplier capacity before demand increases. Marvell's ability to meet these goals will depend on how well it executes.

Wall Street responded to Marvell's long-term outlook by raising its price targets. TD Cowen upgraded Marvell to "Buy" with a $350 target, while Piper Sandler, Needham, and Bank of America subsequently raised their targets to $400. Meanwhile, Oppenheimer and RBC Capital increased the target price to $425.

Despite the broader AI selloff, MRVL stock has climbed 169% so far this year. The average target price for the stock is $337.05, pointing to a possible 42% gain. Jefferies has assigned the highest estimate of $450, which would mean a potential 90% rally from current levels. Overall, most analysts are still strongly bullish about MRVL stock. Out of 39 analysts, 30 rate it as a "Strong Buy," three call it a "Moderate Buy," and six rate it a "Hold."

The Bottom Line on MRVL Stock

Marvell has set a bold financial target, raising expectations. Its stock trades at 56 times projected 2027 earnings, so investors are paying a premium for the hope of higher growth in the future. This also puts MRVL stock at risk if growth slows or the company does not meet its lofty goals. The recent rebound is an encouraging sign, but the next earnings reports will show whether the company is making progress toward management's goals.

news.Title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
news.Content:
By Phoebe Seers and Elizabeth Howcroft

LONDON/PARIS, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Financial regulators in Europe are questioning Google after a cloud computing outage on Tuesday left millions of bank customers without access to ‌key financial services for hours.

The European Banking Authority said that it has been in contact with ‌Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the ​EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters.

Alphabet's Google said the disruption, which lasted several hours, was caused by a "power event" in a London-based network that serves customers across Europe. Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC were among the banks affected.

Lloyds and HSBC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Google spokesperson said: "We have resolved a disruption to ‌Google Cloud services at a third-party ⁠facility in our europe-west2 cloud region due to a power event. Services have been restored. We will update our public status dashboard with an analysis."

At Revolut, which has around ⁠13 million UK customers, a wide range of services including logging in, card payments and cash withdrawals were affected on Tuesday, according to the bank's website.

Revolut said in a statement that it was reviewing the incident to reduce the impact ​of ​any future third-party disruptions, and that customer funds and data ​had remained safe throughout.

The outage is the ‌first major test of new rules across Europe designed to strengthen the resilience of technology providers, including cloud firms, on which the financial sector depends.

The European Union last year designated 19 technology firms as critical third-party providers to the financial sector, bringing them under joint direct oversight of three financial regulators — including the EBA — for the first time. Britain took similar steps for four cloud providers, citing the risk that an outage at a ‌major supplier could affect multiple financial firms at the same ​time. Google Cloud falls under both regulatory frameworks.

In Britain, parliament's Treasury ​Committee has written to the Bank of England ​and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), seeking details of the regulators' response to the outage ‌on Tuesday, the scale of the disruption and ​any financial harm caused.

The FCA ​said it was engaging with Google over the incident. Under Britain's critical third party regime, designated providers like Google Cloud must report serious outages to the FCA and the BoE.

Story Continues

A spokesperson for the Bank ​of England declined to comment.

Under UK ‌rules, banks ultimately are responsible for the services they provide to customers, including when they ​rely on third-party providers.

(Reporting by Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris and Phoebe Seers in London; additional reporting ​by Lawrence White in London; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria)

news.Title: Alphabet (GOOGL): Does Its Valuation Account for Waymo’s Potential?
news.Content:
Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) can finance Waymo from a much larger advertising and cloud business. That gives it room to build autonomous transportation, but the investment is not free. The question is whether growing profits can absorb heavy infrastructure spending while Waymo works toward a lasting business model.

At roughly 23 times forward earnings, the existing businesses must justify the price before investors give much value to future robotaxi profits. For alternatives to Alphabet's Waymo investment, compare the 10 Best Autonomous Vehicle Stocks to Buy Now.

More Rides Must Eventually Mean Better Economics

Autonomous ride-hailing can spread vehicle and technology costs across more paid trips. But entering a city also takes local operating support, fleet capacity, maintenance, and proof that customers will use the service again and again.

Waymo's February expansion announcement described launches for selected riders in four more cities. Its leadership targeted more than one million weekly rides by year-end. That target shows the ambition, but it does not tell us how many rides Waymo has reached.

The Core Business Is Still Funding the Opportunity

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL )'s July 22 earnings release reported second-quarter revenue growth of 24% to $119.8 billion. Search revenue rose 17%, and Google Cloud revenue rose 82% to $24.8 billion.

Waymo combines fleet development with a large corporate backer. Our autonomous driving stocks list compares other routes into this market.

Operating income rose 30% to $40.8 billion. The operating margin reached 34%, which means Alphabet kept about 34 cents of each revenue dollar as operating profit.

Those figures counter the view that new AI products must immediately undermine the existing business. Search and Cloud kept growing, and that gives Alphabet resources to fund new services.

Waymo sits within Other Bets, which reported $382 million in revenue and a $1.8 billion operating loss. Those are combined segment figures, not Waymo's own results. Still, they show that this part of Alphabet consumes earnings and does not support group profit.

Investment Has Begun to Absorb More Cash

The quarterly filing shows that the spending test goes beyond Waymo. Alphabet generated $39.1 billion in operating cash in Q2 but spent $44.9 billion on property and equipment. Free cash flow therefore fell below zero for the quarter.

That does not mean the underlying businesses stopped generating cash. It means investment exceeded the operating cash available in that period.

Story Continues

More rides matter only if the economics work. Compare companies pursuing commercial deployment in our self-driving car stocks list.

New infrastructure could support future revenue. The risk is that capacity and operating costs rise before customers generate enough extra profit. Waymo adds another demand on capital inside that wider investment program.

The strongest buying argument therefore rests on profitable core growth. It does not rest on treating all new infrastructure and robotaxi activity as immediately valuable.

Reported Earnings Make the P/E Look Cheaper

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) trades at 17.62 times trailing earnings and 22.83 times forward earnings. The forward figure means investors pay roughly $23 for each $1 of annual earnings analysts expect.

The forward multiple is higher here, not lower. Alphabet's second-quarter release identified $99 billion of gains on equity securities, which added $6.26 to quarterly EPS. That makes trailing reported earnings a poor standalone measure of recurring profit.

The forward P/E sits below the 28.01 it showed on December 31, 2025, but above the 18.90 on June 30, 2025. The historical comparison does not support a simple claim that the stock is cheap.

Alphabet's spending challenge extends beyond Waymo. Our AI stocks to buy and hold offers a wider comparison of businesses pursuing AI growth.

The communications-sector median is 12.75 times forward adjusted earnings, and Alphabet's multiple is higher. Search scale and cloud growth support a premium, while heavy spending and uncertain returns from newer businesses limit the case for paying it.

Market Sentiment

At the end of Q2 2026, 275 hedge funds held Alphabet's Class A shares, up from 265 in Q1. Their combined stakes totaled $93.74 billion, up from $72.41 billion. Class C holdings are separate.

Does Waymo Strengthen the Buying Case?

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL )'s core growth supports holding the shares, but Waymo alone does not justify a stronger purchase recommendation. Investors already pay a premium while infrastructure spending absorbs substantial cash and Other Bets keeps losing money. Better cash conversion alongside sustained Search and Cloud growth would strengthen the case for adding shares. If investment keeps growing faster than recurring profits, more robotaxi activity will not fix the valuation problem.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of GOOGL as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Content:
Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) gives investors exposure to autonomous driving through Zoox, but the investment case still rests on the businesses that pay for that expansion. Cloud computing and retail must earn enough profit to cover heavy spending before robotaxis add anything meaningful to earnings.

At roughly 24 times forward earnings, the question is whether Amazon can turn its growing operations into stronger cash generation while it funds new bets. See where Amazon's Zoox investment fits among the 10 Best Autonomous Vehicle Stocks to Buy Now .

Zoox Adds Opportunity Before It Adds Proven Earnings

Autonomous ride-hailing could bring in recurring revenue, but running a fleet takes more than good driving software. Vehicles need cleaning, maintenance, charging, and customer support, and enough paying passengers must cover those costs.

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN )'s July earnings release reported that regulators approved Zoox to charge for rides. That clears a commercial hurdle, but it does not prove profitable operations or a material earnings contribution.

Zoox's discussion of fleet data and operations shows how much work remains to improve service. Zoox must turn that operational learning into repeat customer demand before it creates financial value.

AWS Provides the Stronger Financial Foundation

Second-quarter sales rose 20% to $200.6 billion, and operating income rose 43% to $27.5 billion. AWS revenue rose 37% to $42.2 billion, and its operating income reached $16.6 billion.

Zoox is one route into this market. Our autonomous driving stocks list compares vehicle developers with suppliers of the underlying technology.

Cloud demand therefore drives near-term earnings more than Zoox does. Profit grew faster than sales, which means Amazon keeps more of each sales dollar after operating expenses.

These results let Amazon fund Zoox without relying on immediate robotaxi profits. But they also show why valuing Amazon mainly around autonomous driving would miss the businesses that produce today's earnings.

Rising Profit Has Not Prevented a Cash Squeeze

The quarterly filing shows why investment spending is the strongest objection. Operating cash flow rose to $161.4 billion over the twelve months ended June 30, but free cash flow turned negative at $7.6 billion as spending on property and equipment grew.

Free cash flow is the operating cash left after the company's defined capital spending. The contrast shows that stronger operating performance does not automatically leave more money for shareholders.

Story Continues

AWS helps finance Amazon's expansion. Compare other businesses pursuing computing demand in our AI stocks to buy and hold .

Amazon mainly blamed AI investment for the higher spending. Zoox adds another business that must eventually justify the resources it uses, though it did not cause the overall cash flow decline.

Management's third-quarter operating income outlook of $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion supports continued operating strength. The next test is whether that strength improves cash generation after investment.

The Higher Forward P/E Needs a Different Explanation

Amazon trades at 20.05 times trailing earnings and 23.64 times forward earnings. The forward figure means investors pay about $24 for each $1 of annual profit analysts expect.

The forward multiple is higher, so the usual story of expected earnings growth lowering the P/E does not apply. Amazon reported $53.4 billion of second-quarter non-operating pre-tax income, mostly from its Anthropic investments. That calls for caution in treating trailing reported profit as recurring earnings.

The forward P/E has dropped from 34.01 on June 30, 2025. The price investors assign to forecast earnings has eased while cloud profitability has improved, though the figures alone cannot separate share price moves from forecast revisions.

The consumer-discretionary-sector median is 15.40 times forward adjusted earnings, and Amazon's multiple stays higher. AWS and its wider service businesses support a premium, but neither they nor Zoox make every investment attractive.

Amazon's improving cloud profitability supports holding the shares, but negative free cash flow makes a new purchase less compelling at this valuation. Zoox adds potential earnings. news.Title: AppLovin vs. Pinterest: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As the digital advertising market evolves, investors are weighing the explosive growth of AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) against the social commerce potential of Pinterest (NYSE:PINS). Which stock is the better buy?

AppLovin provides the behind-the-scenes software that helps mobile apps grow and make money, while Pinterest is a visual discovery engine where users plan their future purchases. Both companies thrive on advertiser spending, but they offer very different risk and reward profiles for investors looking to capitalize on the next wave of ad-tech innovation.

The case for AppLovin

AppLovin provides software tools for mobile app developers and recently divested its internal apps business to focus on advertising technology. Its platform uses AI-driven bidding to help clients like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) reach users across global mobile games. Many of its clients are also competitors, which creates a complex relationship dynamic and means revenue can be sensitive to industry shifts.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $5.5 billion, marking a significant 70% increase over the previous year. This growth helped the company achieve net income of approximately $3.3 billion, which represents a net margin of 60.8%. This is a strong improvement from the 49% net margin recorded in the prior fiscal year, reflecting higher profitability at scale.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 1.7x, meaning total debt is 1.7 times the value of shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, was healthy at 3.3x. Free cash flow, calculated as operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, reached close to $3.9 billion for the fiscal year.

The case for Pinterest

Pinterest operates a visual discovery platform where over 619 million monthly active users find inspiration for shopping and DIY projects. It makes money primarily through advertising, particularly in the retail and consumer packaged goods sectors. The company has focused on making its pins more shoppable to better compete among tech stocks that bridge social media and commerce.

In FY 2025, revenue grew to approximately $4.2 billion, representing an increase of nearly 15.8% year over year. The company reported net income of roughly $416.9 million for the period, resulting in a net margin of 9.9%. While the company is profitable, its net margin is lower than its peer in this comparison as it continues to invest in platform updates.

Pinterest maintains a very conservative balance sheet as of its December 2025 reporting, with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.1x. The current ratio, measuring short-term liquidity, was exceptionally high at 7.6x, indicating a large cushion of assets to cover near-term obligations. However, stock-based compensation represented roughly 68.6% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Story Continues

Risk profile comparison

AppLovin faces risks from third-party mobile platforms like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Alphabet, which control privacy policies that can limit data availability for ad targeting. The company is also dealing with several securities class action lawsuits and a legal challenge regarding the distribution of inappropriate ads to children. Intense competition from large rivals, including Amazon and Unity Software (NYSE:U), further complicates its market position.

Pinterest depends heavily on its ability to keep users engaged, as its revenue is tied to the size and activity of its user base. The company is vulnerable to changes in search engine algorithms and mobile operating system policies that restrict how it tracks user behavior. It also relies on Amazon for its cloud infrastructure and faces ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding data privacy and content moderation for younger users.

Pinterest carries a lower P/S ratio , reflecting sales over the past twelve months, while AppLovin trades at a higher Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

I'd go with AppLovin. Its AI-powered platform is delivering the results that advertisers want, and they keep coming back for more. In Q2 2026, revenue grew more than 50% year over year and the underlying profitability was exceptional, though revenue came in slightly below analyst expectations and the stock fell sharply after the report, a reminder that expectations for this company run very high.

Pinterest is interesting to me as a long-term story. It reaches 640 million monthly users who come specifically to discover and shop for unique goods, which gives advertisers something valuable: intent. Revenue grew 18% in Q2 2026 and AI is improving how ads perform on the platform. The opportunity in social commerce with this company can't be dismissed.

The honest challenge with Pinterest is that converting that engaged audience into consistent profits has taken longer than investors expected. The company is still posting GAAP net losses while AppLovin generates substantial free cash flow. For me, owning the platform already delivering on its promise feels like the stronger starting point. Look for Q3 results from Pinterest on Oct. 29 and AppLovin on Nov. 4

news.Title: Amazon vs. Alphabet: Is GOOGL’s Cloud Growth Being Undervalued?
news.Content:
Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) have reached such a point in their AI investment cycle where their cloud divisions are becoming more profitable, just as the companies are spending so much on infrastructure that cash flow looks considerably less impressive.

The stocks, meanwhile, are priced remarkably alike. Yahoo Finance's latest available valuation data puts Amazon at 23.64 times forward earnings and Alphabet at 22.83 times. That small premium for Amazon raises a better question than which company has the bigger cloud business: which company is getting more earnings from the money it is putting to work?

In other news, we meticulously compiled a list of the best big name stocks to buy according to financial media, and there are eight stocks other than AMZN and GOOGL that rank in that list. Access the complete list for free here.

Bull Case

Amazon has the larger cloud operation. The company reported that AWS generated $42.2 billion in second-quarter sales, up 37% year-over-year, marking its fastest growth in 18 quarters according to management. Operating income climbed to $16.6 billion from $10.2 billion a year earlier. AWS supplied a significant chunk of Amazon's total operating profit despite accounting for only 21% of sales. That is why the cloud division warrants more attention than its relatively modest share of consolidated revenue suggests. In other news, an ex-Google researcher said AI could "Kill Us All". Should Alphabet investors care? Read here.

But Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) is making that comparison less comfortable for Amazon. Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion, and operating income rose from $2.8 billion to $8.8 billion. AWS remained substantially larger and more profitable in absolute dollars, but Google Cloud's faster growth and widening margin give investors a reason to reassess the gap between the two businesses.

The companies' other operations make the valuation comparison even less straightforward. Amazon's North American retail segment earned $9.1 billion in operating income, up from $7.5 billion, while its advertising business grew 26% year-over-year, according to management. Alphabet's Google Search and other revenue rose 17% to $63.3 billion. Search remains a substantial source of revenue alongside Cloud, and Alphabet's consolidated operating income increased 30% to $40.8 billion. That combination arguably gives Alphabet more than one established source of operating profits while its cloud business scales. We also shortlisted the best healthcare stocks to buy according to hedge funds. Check out the complete list here to make an informed decision .

Story Continues

Bear Case

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) faces much the same tension, on an even starker quarterly basis. It spent $44.9 billion on property and equipment in the June quarter against $39.1 billion in net cash provided by operating activities, leaving approximately $5.85 billion in negative free cash flow. Its cloud operating profits are genuine, but building the capacity to support further growth is consuming cash faster than operations generated it that quarter.

Neither company's headline net income should settle this debate. Amazon's $62.6 billion quarterly net income included $53.4 billion in pretax non-operating income, primarily associated with Anthropic investments. Alphabet likewise recorded $98 billion in net other income, principally unrealized gains on its equity securities. Those figures can overwhelm the operating picture without telling investors whether cloud infrastructure is earning an adequate return.

Conclusion

Amazon's modest forward valuation premium is not obviously explained by AWS's lead in absolute profits alone. Alphabet's Cloud business is narrowing that operating gap while Search continues to deliver substantial revenue, and yet neither deserves a free pass on capital spending. The eventual valuation case for both depends on retaining more cash from each additional dollar of demand, which is, no doubt, less glamorous than AI revenue growth.

news.Title: Amazon (AMZN): Can Custom AI Silicon Outpace Capex Commitments?
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) opened its Trainium AI chips to every PyTorch developer on Monday. Engineers can now run their existing code on Amazon's own hardware without rewriting it. That matters because Amazon's chips business already sells at an annual pace above $25 billion, and Amazon Web Services is growing faster than it has in 18 quarters. But the AI build-out behind that growth has used so much cash that free cash flow turned negative over the past 12 months.

Amazon sells goods to shoppers, collects fees from sellers and Prime members, sells ads to brands, and rents computing power to companies through AWS. The business looks strong enough to carry the spending, but the stock now depends on AWS demand lasting long enough for cash flow to recover. Investors who want more big technology names to follow can find Amazon in our recent list 10 Best Future Stocks to Buy for the Next 5 Years .

AWS Has Sped Up Sharply in a Year

AWS sales grew 37% in the second quarter, up from 17% in the same quarter of 2025. CEO Andy Jassy said the AI business has passed the same $25 billion annual run rate as chips, and both are growing by triple-digit percentages. Anthropic and OpenAI have also made multi-year commitments to Trainium, according to Amazon, which gives that capacity named buyers. If you're interested in AI investing, we recently compiled a report on 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy in October .

Stores and Ads Keep the Core Strong

Advertising sales rose 26% to $19.8 billion in the second quarter. Revenue has grown about 13.2% a year over the past five years, and that record sits on $775.68 billion in sales over the past 12 months. Guidance for the third quarter calls for sales growth of 9% to 12%, which looks slower than the second quarter's 20%. But the company said growth would be nearly 400 basis points higher without Prime Day's effect in both years.

Spending Has Pushed Free Cash Flow Below Zero

Free cash flow was an outflow of $7.6 billion over the past 12 months, compared with an inflow of $18.2 billion a year earlier. Operating cash flow rose 33%, so the business is producing more cash, but spending on property and equipment, mostly for AI, rose even more.

Long-term debt stood at $128.9 billion at the end of the second quarter, up from $65.6 billion at the end of last year. Second-quarter net income of $62.6 billion included $53.4 billion of pre-tax other income, mostly from Anthropic investments. Operating income of $27.5 billion, up 43%, is the cleaner gauge of the business. Those facts limit the story without undoing it, because operating profit is rising and large AI labs have committed to the capacity being built. For someone holding the stock, that means owning a profit story that still depends on those commitments turning into cash.

Story Continues

Investors Are Pricing Amazon on AWS Growth

The stock trades at 30.09 times forward earnings, about 95% above the sector median of 15.40. A forward P/E divides the share price by the profit analysts expect per share, so it shows what investors pay today for each dollar of expected earnings. It rests on adjusted earnings estimates, which matters because reported profit this year includes the Anthropic gain.

Against its own history the stock looks cheaper, since the five-year average is 158.74 and the stock sits about 81% below it. That average is stretched, though, because Amazon earned very little per share early in the window, so almost any price looked high. Against the sector, the premium shows investors are paying up for AWS growth.

Hedge fund interest kept growing, with 369 funds holding Amazon at the end of the second quarter against 353 in the first, even as free cash flow turned negative. For investors tracking hedge fund interest in cloud computing, our list of 10 Best Cloud Computing Stocks to Buy According to Hedge Funds covers more names. Short interest is only 0.88% of the float, which means that share of freely traded stock has been borrowed and sold in hopes of buying it back cheaper. That small a number suggests doubts about the spending show up mostly in the multiple, not in bets that the stock will fall.

That brings the story back to the chip news, because more developers on Trainium could add demand for the capacity Amazon is paying for. Cash flow can catch up if AWS keeps growing near its current pace, since the business already produces more cash each year and mainly needs the spending to level off. The third-quarter report next week will show whether the outflow is shrinking and whether AWS holds its pace.

news.Title: 1 Number Every UPS Investor Should Watch in Q3 Earnings
news.Content:
In the case of United Parcel Service (NYSE: UPS), it's all about adjusted operating profit margin. This key number lies at the heart of the company's transformational strategy, which entails reducing less-profitable Amazon deliveries in favor of higher-margin e-commerce deliveries, particularly in targeted markets such as healthcare and small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs).

At the same time, UPS's investments in smart facilities and automation are intended to improve productivity and, ultimately, margins. Everything points to margin expansion, but is it working out like that for UPS right now? Let's find out.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

UPS changes guidance

In the fourth-quarter earnings presentation in January, management forecast full-year revenue of $89.7 billion and an adjusted operating profit margin of 9.6%, implying $8.611 billion in adjusted operating profit. The headline guidance was maintained on the first-quarter earnings call in April. Still, on the second-quarter earnings call, management increased its full-year revenue guidance to $91.2 billion and specifically said that adjusted operating profit would be about $8.65 billion.

Why the guidance change isn't good news

Superficially, it's an increase in revenue guidance and also an increase over the implied guidance of $8.611 billion I calculated above. However, there are two key considerations for investors, and they matter a lot for the upcoming results of a company with a near-7% dividend yield .

First, the new guidance implies an adjusted operating margin of 9.48%, down from the 9.6% initially forecast. Second, it's important to understand the nuance of the guidance change. As previously discussed, due to rising fuel costs, UPS raised fuel surcharges by $1.173 billion in the first half. Bearing in mind that the increase in full-year revenue guidance was $1.5 billion to $91.2 billion, it's reasonable to expect a large chunk of the revenue increase is due to the fuel surcharge.

Turning to the difficult question of how much profit UPS is making from the fuel surcharges, its fuel cost and third-party costs increased by $744 million, resulting in a net difference of $429 million -- a figure slightly more than the increase in adjusted operating profit guidance.

To be clear, management's position is that the fuel surcharge is intended solely to cover increased fuel costs, and there are associated costs related to fuel disruptions as well. Moreover, CFO Brian Dykes argued that "the net impact to consolidated operating profit dollars was modest" on the second-quarter earnings call.

Story Continues

In the absence of knowing exactly what kind of figure "modest" implies, it could be argued that the combination of a positive contribution from fuel surcharges over fuel cost -- something not likely to prove sustainable -- actually implies a significant decrease in adjusted operating profit margin if the impact of fuel is taken out.

The key metric to look out for

As noted, this is the year when UPS should start to build on margin improvement, not least because it finished the so-called "glide down" of Amazon deliveries by 50% (volume) from the start of 2025 to the middle of 2026. That's why investors are so focused on margin, particularly the expected adjusted operating profit margin in the U.S. domestic package segment.

I've replicated what the Wall Street consensus, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence , is expecting for the segment, and the company's total adjusted operating margins will be below. news.Title: Cisco (CSCO): Can It Profit From Helping Customers Spend Less on AI?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO ), included in Insider Monkey's 10 Best Pick and Shovel AI Stocks to Buy for the Long Term , has another way to benefit from AI investment: helping customers control their operating costs. Agents can repeatedly call models and retry tasks, creating unpredictable bills. Monitoring that waste could support lasting software demand.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) has a forward P/E of 20x and a trailing P/E of 32x. Trailing P/E uses earnings from the past twelve months; forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) has a forward P/E of 39x. Its latest quarterly GAAP operating margin was 45%, versus 25% here, supporting a premium. The lower valuation looks reasonable if earnings growth becomes dependable cash generation.

For Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO), the midpoint of management's separate fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $5.05–$5.11 implies approximately 17% growth from $4.33 in fiscal 2026. Networking revenue grew 22%, supporting the outlook. Fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS was $3.33; adjustments included stock compensation, acquisition amortization, and restructuring. Reported earnings also benefited from investment gains excluded from management's adjusted results. These accounting effects are separate from expected operating growth. Software deserves valuation weight when recurring relationships produce cash after reinvestment .

AI Complexity Creates a Monitoring Problem

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) has added Tokenomics capabilities to Splunk Agent Observability, connecting AI usage and spending with agent performance. Customers can identify expensive workflows and compare model cost with quality. Switching routine tasks to cheaper models could reduce bills while preserving useful output. Monitoring remains necessary as applications and models change.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) can bring network information into those investigations and sell through established enterprise relationships. Integrating monitoring into operating routines could lower selling costs and support renewals. The commercial test is whether AI adoption expands recurring customer spending .

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) still has work to do. Fiscal 2026 software revenue rose 4% to $23.2 billion, while total subscription revenue increased just 1%. Observability revenue also grew 4%, but network assurance supplied the growth while the observability suite declined. New monitoring features need to reverse that decline before they can change the earnings mix.

Story Continues

Customers Must Save More Than They Pay

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) prices Agent Observability around spans, which record individual workflow operations, with included evaluation capacity and optional additional resources. Cheaper models can lower customers' token bills without reducing monitored activity. Eliminating unnecessary workflow steps, however, could constrain billable usage. Expanding coverage and retaining customers must compensate. Customers should measure savings after monitoring fees and integration work, while preserving task quality.

Dynatrace, Inc. (NYSE:DT), with a forward P/E of 30x, offers competing AI cost and performance tools. Its predominantly subscription-based business helps explain its premium. Collecting, storing and evaluating more data also costs money. Higher monitoring volumes create value only if subscription revenue grows faster than delivery and development costs.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $12.8 billion of fiscal 2026 free cash flow, down 4%, after deducting capital spending from operating cash flow. Higher capital spending and a final $2.3 billion transition-tax payment weighed on cash generation. Inventory absorbed $2.54 billion, while financing receivables absorbed $1.84 billion across the business. Equipment supply and customer financing tie up cash before collections arrive.

Inventory purchase commitments reached $17.17 billion, versus $7.60 billion, reflecting hyperscaler demand and higher memory prices. Supplying AI infrastructure requires more upfront investment. Delayed shipments could postpone collections; weaker demand could leave expensive components unused and force write-downs that reduce margins. Year-end debt was $29.5 billion, against $15.9 billion of cash and investments. Shareholders need software growth that strengthens cash conversion .

Conclusion

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) looks fairly valued at 20x forward earnings. Helping customers spend less on AI can become profitable recurring business when savings support renewals and broader adoption. Sustaining the valuation requires delivery of the earnings outlook, stronger subscription growth, and cash conversion after investment. A higher software premium needs improving monitoring revenue and margins; useful dashboards alone will not earn it.

news.Title: 亞太科技股迎最強動能！摩根看好台韓半導體與高階科技 日元匯率估155-160
news.Content:
摩根資產管理發布第4季投資展望，摩根投信環球市場策略師林雅慧今（21）日表示，亞太市場具備強勁成長潛力，其中台灣與韓國的半導體及高階科技產業受惠於人工智慧（AI）需求，展現營運韌性與成長動能。此外，日本企業持續推動改革，加上內需復甦與薪資成長，也使日股成為國際資金關注的市場。

林雅慧指出，儘管全球總體經濟仍存在不確定性，AI需求依舊是推動經濟成長的重要動能，不僅帶動科技巨頭獲利成長，也為整體供應鏈提供實質支撐。台灣與韓國在半導體及高階科技製造領域具備競爭優勢，隨著企業獲利預期持續上修，科技類股仍是投資組合中重要的成長配置。

除了台韓科技股，日本市場也是投資焦點之一。林雅慧表示，日本企業近年持續推動公司治理改革、提升股東權益報酬率（ROE），加上內需逐漸復甦及薪資成長，有助於吸引國際資金流入日股。

匯率方面，林雅慧預期，短期日圓走勢仍受到美日利差及總體經濟環境影響，美元兌日圓可能在155至160區間震盪。日圓若維持相對弱勢，有助於日本出口企業維持獲利表現，為日股提供基本面支撐。

資產配置方面，林雅慧建議，面對高利率與市場波動，投資人除布局AI科技股，也可適度配置中短天期公債，以掌握相對具吸引力的殖利率，並透過不同類型的債券及信貸資產分散風險。此外，東南亞、日本等區域市場也各具投資機會，建議透過跨區域及跨資產配置，分散投資組合風險，掌握不同市場的成長與收益機會。

news.Title: Jim Cramer and Ken Fisher’s AI Pick: Microsoft (MSFT)
news.Content:
Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has gone almost nowhere over the past twelve months, with the stock up about 2% in that period. The stock ranks second on our list of the top 10 stocks Jim Cramer and billionaire Ken Fisher like . The company reports its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on October 28, so can the stock gain in the coming weeks? Let's analyze as the earnings date nears.

How Microsoft Makes Money From AI

Microsoft earns AI revenue in two main places. Microsoft 365 Copilot is an AI assistant inside Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams that companies pay for per employee. It passed 30 million paid seats in the fiscal fourth quarter. Azure, Microsoft's cloud, rents computing power and AI models to businesses, and its revenue grew 43% in that quarter. Microsoft also holds a financial stake in OpenAI, whose products run on Azure first.

Microsoft sells new AI tools faster than most rivals because its software already runs inside almost every large company, so customers skip the long process of approving a new vendor. Its commercial backlog, which is signed business not yet delivered, rose 84%, or 25% without OpenAI. See whether the spending is paying off.

Will AI Agents Replace the Office Seat?

This is the biggest worry on the software side. Most of Microsoft's revenue and profit still come from software sold per user. If AI agents do office work, companies need fewer employee seats, and Microsoft itself expects seat growth to slow over time. Microsoft has three answers. Companies need cloud computing to run AI agents, and Azure rents it out. Its customers' work data already sits in Microsoft's systems, which AI agents need to do useful work. Microsoft is also building its own AI models, expected by 2027, to cut what it pays outside AI providers when people use Copilot.

Impax Global Environmental Markets Fund described the same selloff in its investor letter. Click to read the full letter.

Capacity, Chips and OpenAI

Capacity is the first open question. Bloomberg reported that Microsoft restricted new cloud subscriptions at key data center hubs in the US and Europe because it lacked capacity. Morgan Stanley estimates Microsoft added about 3.25 gigawatts of capacity in fiscal 2026 and expects about 4.25 gigawatts in fiscal 2027.

Chips are the second. Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 AI chip this month and says it delivers 40% more output per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Production starts early next year. The chip could reduce Microsoft's reliance on Nvidia, but earlier Maia versions shipped only in limited volumes.

Story Continues

OpenAI is the third. It makes up a large part of the backlog, which is why the 84% growth drops to 25% without it. A change in that relationship would hit Microsoft's AI sales.

What Wall Street Wants to See on October 28

Microsoft has beaten earnings estimates in each of the last four quarters. The stock has rebounded in recent weeks, so Morgan Stanley says it faces a higher bar. The firm rates Microsoft Overweight and wants to see Azure growth in the mid-40s, better monetization of Microsoft 365 and Copilot, and disciplined operating expenses. The stock is up about 40% over the past six months, so investors expect a clean report. Check out the full analysis here.

Three Ways the Report Could Land

If Azure grows 44% to 45% or faster and Microsoft shows Copilot use deepening, the rally has support. If Azure lands on guidance but capital spending rises faster than cash flow and Microsoft gives no new Copilot data, the stock could stall, since expectations have moved up. If Azure growth falls short, capacity limits persist or OpenAI news hits the backlog, the AI-spending worry that sent shares down after the fiscal 2026 third-quarter report could return. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has beaten earnings estimates four quarters in a row, and the market will want to see a fifth.

news.Title: KLA (KLAC) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 28, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This maker of equipment for manufacturing semiconductors is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.18 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +34.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $4.05 billion, up 26.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.28% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Story Continues

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for KLA?

For KLA, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.03%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that KLA will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that KLA would post earnings of $1 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.05, delivering a surprise of +5.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

KLA doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Title: UPS to Report Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
United Parcel Service UPS is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 27, before the market opens. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the to-be-reported quarter's earnings per share and revenues is pegged at $1.63 and $22.23 billion, respectively.

The bottom-line projection indicates a year-over-year decline of 6.3%. The consensus mark for the to-be-reported quarter has remained stable over the past 60 days. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for quarterly revenues implies a year-over-year expansion of 3.8%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

For 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for UPS' revenues is pegged at $91.71 billion, implying a 3.4% year-over-year uptick. The consensus mark for 2026 EPS is pegged at $7.19, indicating a year-over-year improvement of 0.4%.

This package delivery company's earnings beat estimates each of the past four quarters, with the average surprise being 12.4%.

United Parcel Service, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

United Parcel Service, Inc. price-eps-surprise | United Parcel Service, Inc. Quote

Q3 Earnings Whispers for UPS

Our proven model predicts an earnings beat for UPS for the September quarter. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the odds of an earnings beat. That is exactly the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

UPS has an Earnings ESP of +0.95% and a Zacks Rank #3. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Shaping UPS' Quarterly Performance

We expect the still-ongoing macro uncertainty due to the Middle East conflict to have dented UPS' performance in the September quarter. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has resulted in a sharp jump in oil prices. This has been naturally hurting the bottom line of transportation stocks, like UPS. This is because fuel expenses represent a key input cost for a transportation company.

UPS' decision to scale back business with Amazon AMZN is expected to have kept third-quarter volumes muted. Management reached an agreement in principle with Amazon to reduce the e-commerce giant's volume by more than 50% by June 2026. CEO Carol Tome noted that Amazon was not the company's most profitable customer. The reduction in volumes is compelling UPS to right-size its network. We expect overall volumes to decline 5.4% year over year in the September quarter.

That said, third-quarter results are likely to reflect UPS' efforts toward improving profitability over sheer volume, through its "Better, Not Bigger" strategy. Under the cost-cutting initiatives, UPS has substantially reduced its U.S. operational workforce and closed daily operations at multiple leased and owned buildings. Moreover, UPS has been focusing on increasing automation in sorting and operations and leveraging AI for logistics planning to boost efficiency.

Story Continues

The shift in focus toward higher-margin areas such as small and medium-sized businesses or SMBs and healthcare logistics from low-margin volumes (like Amazon) is expected to be reflected in UPS' first-quarter results. Notably, SMBs contributed 34.5% to total U.S. volume in the June quarter, reflecting a 250-basis-point year-over-year improvement. We expect SMBs to have performed strongly in the September quarter as well, boosting results.

UPS Underperforms on Price Front

Shares of UPS have declined marginally year to date ("YTD"), similar to the Zacks Transportation-Air Freight and Cargo industry. Shares of rival FedEx FDX have seen a single-digit (% -wise) rise in the same timeframe.

YTD Price Comparison

On the basis of the forward 12-month Price/Sales (P/S), UPS' shares are trading at a discount compared with the industry average. FedEx is cheaper. UPS and FedEx each currently have a Value Score of B.

Investment Thesis for UPS Stock

UPS is looking to grow its per-package revenues by gaining more business in segments like healthcare. A few years back, UPS acquired Bomi Group, an industry-leading multinational healthcare logistics provider. Last year, UPS acquired Andlauer Healthcare Group as part of its commitment to offer global specialty capabilities.

Because of this strategic shift, UPS did not increase its quarterly dividend this year, keeping it at $6.56 annually. In the event of the company failing to put an end to its struggles through the strategic shift, the high payout ratio may lead to a dividend cut, which would be disastrous for dividend investors.

End Note

It is worth noting that the company has the brand and the network to continue generating steady cash flows in the long run. This makes UPS a compelling long-term player in the transportation space. However, the near-term headwinds, including the macro uncertainties and volume declines, are hard to ignore.

So, all in all, it is worth holding on to UPS stock for now. Betting on the stock ahead of its upcoming results does not seem like a good idea. It is better to wait for management's commentary on volumes and cost-cutting efforts, apart from the updated 2026 guidance, to get more clarity on near-term prospects.

news.Title: Can Netlist's New LIGHTNING ULL DDR5 Boost Its AI Market Reach?
news.Content:
Netlist Inc . NLST recently announced next-generation LIGHTNING Ultra-Low Latency ("ULL") DDR5 RDIMMs for Agentic AI workstations and servers. The DDR5-6000 and DDR5-6400 products are designed to boost responsiveness in memory-sensitive AI and enterprise workloads.

The latest modules feature a JEDEC-compatible "drop-in architecture" supporting qualified deployments on AMD and Intel server platforms.

Netlist highlighted that internal testing demonstrated up to 10% lower loaded memory latency compared with conventional DDR5 RDIMMs, potentially improving performance in latency-sensitive applications.

The new products target agentic AI workstations and servers, multi-agent systems, retrieval-augmented generation, large language models and vector databases. Applications also extend to high-frequency trading, scientific computing and electronic design automation, cloud infrastructure and data analytics.

Netlist remains focused on portfolio expansion to boost its presence in the AI memory market. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that its Lightning portfolio of overclocked, low-latency DDR5 RDIMM and UDIMM products has been gaining traction. Meanwhile, NLST's CXL NVvault solution is sampling with system-on-chip vendors, hyperscalers and key OEMs for next-generation hardware platforms. Netlist is also upbeat about MRDIMM and high-performance server memory architecture aimed at overcoming the bandwidth limitations of DDR5 RDIMMs. Management, citing industry analysts, noted that MRDIMM could be a $100 billion market by 2030.

Meanwhile, agreements with Micron MU and Samsung also strengthen its IP monetization strategy. The five-year licensing arrangement with Micron provides for $600 million in payments, beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The LIGHTNING expansion could strengthen Netlist's position in AI infrastructure space, although wider adoption and meaningful revenue contributions remain key to its long-term growth prospects amid increasing competition in the semiconductor space.

Competitive Landscape

Netlist operates in a highly competitive memory market alongside established players, including Micron, Samsung Electronics, SK hynix SKHY and Rambus RMBS. While Netlist has recently strengthened its ties with Micron and Samsung through licensing agreements, competition in advanced AI memory technologies remains intense. Rambus represents another notable competitive force, offering DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM interface chipsets for data-center applications.

Last month, Micron demonstrated a 512GB DDR5 RDIMM capable of speeds up to 9,200 MT/s.

Story Continues

A few days back, Rambus unveiled a Power Management IC ("PMIC") solution. PMIC is designed to facilitate low-power, high-performance LPDDR6 Small Outline Compression Attached Memory Modules (SOCAMM2). Earlier in the year, Rambus expanded its DDR5 portfolio with complete DDR5-9600 chipsets for both client and server memory modules.

South Korea-based SK hynix has a strong presence across DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory ("HBM") markets. Recently, SK hynix showcased its next-generation AI memory portfolio, including 256GB DDR5 3DS RDIMM and 128GB DDR5 MRDIMM and 192GB SOCAMM2, at the OCP Global Summit 2026.The company also unveiled the second-generation 256GB CMM-DDR5 solution, offering approximately 30% better energy efficiency and more than twice the bandwidth than its predecessor.

news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 21, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Microsoft MSFT, Palantir Technologies PLTR, Micron Technology MU, Lam Research LRCX and IonQ IONQ

Here are highlights from Tuesday's Analyst Blog:

AI, Semiconductors & Quantum Computing: What Lies in Store for 2027?

Artificial intelligence (AI) has dominated technology investment in 2026, driving heavy spending on data centers, advanced chips and computing infrastructure. Semiconductor demand has benefited from this expansion, particularly in high-bandwidth memory and advanced manufacturing. Quantum computing, meanwhile, remains an emerging investment opportunity, with companies working to turn research breakthroughs and commercial partnerships into viable businesses.

In 2027, investors are expected to focus more on companies that can convert rising demand for AI, semiconductor and quantum technologies into actual revenue and earnings growth.

The scale of investment is substantial. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending of $2.67 trillion in 2026, up 49.5% year over year, in its September report. Its August forecast put global semiconductor revenues at $1.56 trillion in 2026 and $1.94 trillion in 2027. These projections clearly show the economic importance of AI infrastructure. However, they also raise questions about capital efficiency, supply constraints and the sustainability of demand.

Macroeconomic conditions will influence this investment cycle. On Oct. 13, the International Monetary Fund projected global economic growth of 3.1% in 2026, identifying AI investment as a source of support while warning of risks from geopolitical conflict, higher energy prices and rising bond yields. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target range to 3.75%-4% in September, citing elevated inflation. Higher financing costs can weigh on capital-intensive projects and valuations, making investment returns particularly important in 2027.

AI: Monetization Becomes the Key Test

Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending to reach $3.64 trillion in 2027, with AI infrastructure accounting for approximately $1.98 trillion. AI services and software are also projected to expand, reflecting growing efforts to integrate AI into business applications. Gartner has noted that enterprises are increasingly emphasizing cost control, usage tracking and measurable outcomes.

Story Continues

The key question is whether AI-driven revenue growth and productivity gains can justify the substantial investment in computing infrastructure. In 2027, enterprise adoption, inference demand and the deployment of AI agents are expected to be important indicators to watch. Microsoft , through its Azure cloud and AI offerings and Palantir Technologies , through its enterprise AI platform, are two companies investors can monitor for evidence of AI monetization, customer adoption and operating efficiency.

Semiconductors: Memory and Manufacturing Take Center Stage

Gartner projects semiconductor revenues to approach $1.94 trillion in 2027, including $1.08 trillion from memory. This forecast highlights the importance of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), DRAM and NAND alongside AI processors. SEMI separately expects global 300mm fab equipment spending to rise 14% to $151 billion in 2027, supported by advanced-node and memory investment.

These projections create opportunities across foundries, chip-design companies and equipment suppliers. Micron Technology , a major memory-chip manufacturer and Lam Research , a supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, offer exposure to two important parts of this investment cycle.

Quantum Computing: Commercial Progress Remains Uneven

Gartner projects global quantum-computing revenues to reach $1.1 billion in 2027, compared with $869.9 million in 2026. It expects public-sector spending to lead industry demand, reaching $245 million in 2027. These figures suggest a developing market rather than widespread commercial adoption.

Investors can monitor IonQ , which develops trapped-ion quantum computing systems and D-Wave Quantum, which focuses on quantum annealing and related computing solutions.

news.Title: CIEN Wins Space Norway Cable Deal: Can Subsea Networking Drive Growth?
news.Content:
Ciena Corporation CIEN is strengthening its position in the global subsea networking market after securing a turnkey contract from Space Norway to modernize existing subsea cable systems in Svalbard and deploy advanced networking technology for the upcoming Arctic Way system. The project highlights the growing importance of resilient, high-capacity communications infrastructure in remote regions where connectivity is essential for scientific research, government operations and national security.

The agreement combines upgrades to legacy infrastructure with the deployment of a new subsea network expected to enter service in 2028. By supplying optical networking equipment, advanced transponders and network management software, Ciena aims to improve capacity, reliability and operational efficiency across Space Norway's Arctic communications footprint. For Ciena, this approach creates an opportunity to supply technology across multiple routes and potentially support future network extensions.

A key aspect of the deal is Ciena's combination of optical transmission hardware and network management software. The technology is designed to improve network capacity, simplify operations and support reliable data transmission across demanding subsea routes. Ciena 6500 Optical Platform provides optical transport capabilities for high-capacity networks. In the Arctic project, it will support communications across the new and upgraded subsea systems. Its Navigator Network Control Suite also provides visibility and control, helping Space Norway manage operations across its infrastructure while supporting operational redundancy.

The Space Norway agreement fuels Ciena's already strong business momentum, driven by increasing demand for high-speed connectivity and AI infrastructure. Ciena reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $1.67 billion, representing 37% year-over-year growth. It also raised its fiscal 2026 revenue outlook to $6.42 billion (+/-$50 million). For fiscal 2027, management expects at least 30% revenue growth.

CIEN's Optical Growth Faces Competitive Challenges

CIEN continues to strengthen its position in the optical networking market as rising demand for high-capacity connectivity drives investments in digital infrastructure. Recently, Openreach deployed Ciena's Waveserver platform with WaveLogic 6 1.6Tb/s technology to expand its OSEA portfolio, offering high-capacity connectivity across U.K. cable landing stations, data centers and core network nodes. The solution combines 400G and 800G traffic over 1.6Tb/s wavelengths, supporting up to 32 400G services in a compact 2RU chassis.

Story Continues

However, Ciena operates in a competitive optical networking market. Winning contracts does not automatically guarantee attractive margins, especially when turnkey delivery involves substantial execution responsibilities. It faces competition from other optical networking vendors like Corning Incorporated GLW, Cisco Systems CSCO and Nokia NOK.

Assessing CIEN's Market Peers

Cisco's vertically integrated networking stack is expanding across scale-out and scale-across AI architectures. In the fiscal fourth quarter, it won three new hyperscaler designs – a P200 scale-across system, a G200 scale-out system and an optical line system. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics, while Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter. Management has line of sight to multiple additional design wins over the next six months across G300, G200 and P200 systems and optics. In September, management said Cisco supplies chips and full systems to hyperscalers and plans to become independent of merchant silicon providers by fiscal 2029, giving it greater control over product design and supply.

However, the outlook still depends on converting G300, G200, P200 and optics opportunities, and becoming independent of merchant silicon providers by fiscal 2029.

Corning has entered the second half of 2026 with its growth outlook tied to AI infrastructure and optical connectivity. It launched Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 and continues to see opportunities in advanced optics products tied to AI-driven data center build-outs and semiconductor manufacturing demand. Corning is also expanding its GenAI optical portfolio with multicore fiber and high-density connectivity solutions that improve network capacity and reduce installation complexity. Secular demand for bandwidth, cloud computing and AI infrastructure continues to support Corning's Optical Communications business.

GLW also announced a long-term partnership with NVIDIA to expand U.S.-based optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10 times and increase domestic fiber production capacity by more than 50%. In September, Corning secured a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with Verizon to supply more than 80 million miles of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions through 2032, strengthening its long-term revenue visibility and positioning it to benefit from expanding broadband and AI infrastructure demand.

Nokia continues to benefit from its broad portfolio spanning mobile networks, optical transport, IP routing, fixed broadband, software and services. This integrated offering enables the company to address evolving customer requirements across telecommunications operators, enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Network Infrastructure delivered double-digit growth in second-quarter 2026, supported by continued momentum in Optical Networks and IP Networks. The planned divestiture of the Fixed Wireless Access CPE business simplifies the portfolio and allows greater investment in higher-growth opportunities such as AI networking and optical technologies.

While AI and cloud demand is supporting Optical Networks and IP Networks, carrier spending remains mixed across regions and business lines. Management continues to expect stronger performance in the second half of 2026, but quarterly demand patterns remain influenced by customer capital expenditure timing and software revenue recognition. Management noted that supply constraints continue to affect portions of the optical networking market, contributing to long-term customer ordering patterns.

news.Title: 力積電：第4季營收估增2位數　台日星就新廠研調
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年10月21日電）晶圓代工廠力積電 (6770) 預期，第4季3D AI代工營收可望逐漸恢復動能，加上邏輯代工價格調漲，整體季營收可望成長2位數水準。因無塵室空間已用盡，已就新廠規劃於台灣、新加坡及日本等地進行研調。

力積電今天召開線上法人說明會，公布第3季營運結果。受惠產品平均售價上揚，力積電第3季營收攀升至新台幣213億元，季增23%。

因產品平均售價上揚，加上銅鑼廠停線，及整體利用率上升，力積電第3季毛利率48%，較第2季揚升20個百分點，稅後淨利65億元，季增98%，每股純益1.38元，累計前3季每股純益5.42元。

力積電表示，全球動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）市場仍處於供需失衡狀態，隨著DRAM大廠積極拓展高頻寬記憶體（HBM），逐步退出利基型DRAM，需求將持續吃緊，利基型DRAM晶圓代工價格維持高檔。

至於與美光合作的DRAM 1P製程進展順利，機台預計2027年第1季到位，第2季進入試產。

邏輯代工業務方面，力積電指出，下半年晶圓廠產能普遍滿載，成熟製程除2026的代工價格均已全面調漲外，2027亦計劃目標調漲10%至20%，目前已積極與客戶協商以長期合約並綁定2027年的價與量，產能分配會以長期合約客戶優先。

力積電表示，銅鑼廠預計於2027年第1季前完成交接給美光（Micron），2026年下半年受限於銅鑼廠設備大規模停線移機，導致晶圓堆疊及矽中介層在第3季產出明顯下滑，3D AI代工營收同步下降。

隨著晶圓堆疊及矽中介層於新竹廠陸續復線，3DAI代工營收可望自第4季起逐漸恢復動能，並在2027年逐季上揚。此外，邏輯代工價格調漲，預期第4季整體營收可望成長2位數。

力積電指出，因無塵室空間已用盡，已就新廠的規劃，於台灣、新加坡及日本等地進行調研，聚焦在3DAI代工的產能擴張，聯合策略客戶就共同投資的可行性進行評估，以布局2028年之後的市場成長契機。

news.Title: AEIS Rides on Strong Semiconductor Growth: Can It Beat KLAC and MKSI?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy AEIS benefits from strong demand for semiconductor equipment, driven by increasing investments in advanced logic and memory manufacturing. The company's growing adoption of precision power solutions and expanding product portfolio strengthen its competitive position against KLA KLAC and MKS MKSI, which are also benefiting from semiconductor industry growth.

The company reported record semiconductor revenues of $278 million in the second quarter of 2026, increasing 33% year over year and 27% sequentially. Growth was driven by robust demand for leading-edge memory and logic technologies, alongside rising etch and deposition intensity. Management expects semiconductor revenues to increase nearly 50% year over year in the second half of 2026, reflecting sustained customer demand.

AEIS is strengthening its market position through innovative plasma power technologies, including its eVerest and eVoS platforms. These solutions deliver improved yield and throughput for advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes. The company is also gaining traction in system power applications, securing design wins in semiconductor testing, atomic layer deposition and thermal sensing. New product ramps and additional design wins are expected to accelerate revenue growth in 2027 and beyond.

The company's expanding manufacturing footprint is another growth catalyst. AEIS expects to begin generating revenue from its new Thailand facility in the fourth quarter of 2026. Once fully developed, its global manufacturing network is expected to support approximately $5 billion in annual revenue-generating capacity, providing flexibility to address rising semiconductor and data center demand.

AEIS's strong semiconductor revenue growth, expanding product portfolio and improving manufacturing capabilities are expected to boost top-line growth and position it favorably against KLAC and MKSI. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

AEIS Faces Stiff Competition

The company is facing stiff competition from companies like KLA and MKS. Both KLA and MKSI are expanding their footprint in the semiconductor market.

KLA is benefiting from strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in AI infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging.

MKS is benefiting from rising AI-related investment across semiconductor and advanced packaging markets, with demand broadening through memory, logic, advanced PCBs, photonics, and chemistry equipment. Second-quarter 2026 semiconductor revenues rose 28% year over year to $554 million, with broad-based growth across deposition and etch applications. Management expects third-quarter 2026 semiconductor revenues of $630 million (+/- $15 million), implying more than 50% year-over-year growth, supported by a healthy backlog, NAND upgrades, advanced logic and DRAM demand and design wins in dissolved gas and RF power.

Story Continues

news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-21 17:13:24 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股主要指數今(21)日開高走低，收盤全面轉弱。上證指數收於3,713.03點，下跌0.60%，日K翻黑；深證成指收於11,704.35點，下跌0.82%；創業板指收於2,694.71點，下跌1.62%；科創50收於1,343.28點，上漲0.06%，相對抗跌。整體來看，市場呈現明顯的開高走低格局，個股跌多漲少。

依盤勢來看，創業板指今日壓力最大，主要受寧德時代大跌拖累。動力電池鏈、固態電池相關個股同步走弱，帶動創業板指失守2,700點；新能源汽車產業鏈、家電、白酒、煤炭與金融等類股也普遍承壓，放大指數跌勢。成交量方面，滬市今日成交6,428億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交7,866億元，兩市成交額1兆4,294億元，較前一交易日量縮約1%。

從盤面上來看，光通訊、存儲與晶片題材盤中一度走揚，致尚科技、天孚通信、劍橋科技等表現活躍，德明利也帶動存儲族群一度轉強；不過，午後追價力道減弱，科技題材未能把漲勢延續到收盤，科創50因此僅小幅收紅。

此外，數據要素族群今日表現活躍，南威軟件、海量數據、天威視訊、深桑達A等走強；AI漫劇與傳媒影視個股也獲得資金關注。市場同時關注國家數據集團成立，以及工信部研究新一代智慧製造政策，帶動數位經濟與AI+製造相關想像升溫。

銀河證券表示，持續看好A股中長期表現，建議投資者理性看待海外短期擾動。一方面，以紅利資產作為底倉，增強配置的穩健性；另一方面，關注科技族群配置機會，結合第三季財報表現，挖掘產業轉型升級中成長路徑較為清晰、盈利兌現能力較強的優質企業，重點關注前期調整較為充分、股價表現與基本面出現偏離的標的，擇機布局。
