No 'Example Anywhere on the Planet': Billionaire Kevin O'Leary's Utah Data Center Could Use Enough Electricity to Power 16 Million People

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Hotter-than-expected inflation data added further pressure. U.S. annual inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August, raising the prospect of higher interest rates and more expensive financing for the industry's massive infrastructure buildout.

For Oracle, this strikes at the core of its investment case. The sharp selloff, therefore, raises a more fundamental question. Has the decline created an attractive opportunity to invest in the AI expansion? Or is the lower share price a warning of the financial risks? Let's find out.

Oracle's Financial Check

Based in Austin, Texas, Oracle is valued at approximately $387 billion by market capitalization and provides enterprise databases, business applications, and cloud infrastructure for organizations managing data and deploying AI. Beyond its established software business, the company is expanding computing capacity to serve customers requiring infrastructure for demanding AI workloads.

ORCL stock closed on Oct. 16 at $128.23 per share. The stock has declined 33% year-to-date (YTD) and 55% for the past 52 weeks.

At 19.7 times trailing earnings versus the roughly 32 times sector median, Oracle looks cheaper on earnings but pricier on sales at 6 times versus about 3.5 times for the sector. Oracle's $2 annualized dividend also yields approximately 1.49%.

Oracle released first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Sept. 10. Revenue rose 30% year-over-year (YOY) to $19.35 billion, beating the $19.1 billion analyst estimate. Adjusted EPS also increased 30% YOY to $1.92 and exceeded the $1.74 consensus estimate.

Story Continues

That earnings strength extended to operating results. Oracle reported adjusted operating income of $8.15 billion against expectations of $7.8 billion. This was a 4.5% beat, with an adjusted operating margin of roughly 42%.

Cloud infrastructure drove much of the revenue growth, jumping 121% to $7.4 billion. Cloud applications revenue increased 10% to $4.2 billion, while software revenue fell 3% to $5.5 billion.

To support that cloud expansion, the company delivered 850 megawatts of additional data-center capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs. Those GPU deliveries nearly tripled the preceding quarter's total.

Oracle also added more than $30 billion in AI cloud contracts during the quarter. This pushed remaining performance obligations (RPO) to $664 billion, up $209 billion YOY.

However, the expansion continued to weigh on cash flow. Free cash flow fell to -$5.4 billion from -$1.87 billion in the previous quarter.

Oracle's Next Growth Drivers

Oracle's latest product launches and partnerships show where its next phase of growth could come from and what shareholders will help finance. On Sept. 29, Oracle introduced Fusion Claw with 25 new applications, expanding its agentic application portfolio to 75. The technology combines AI reasoning with precise enterprise computation to automate complex tasks under customer-defined controls.

Infrastructure security is advancing, too. On Oct. 13, Oracle, Microsoft (MSFT), and Marvell established an Open Compute Project working group targeting NIST FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security. Their proposed server-integrated security module would protect cryptographic keys where workloads run, reducing network dependence and supporting regulatory compliance.

Oracle also launched Nexus Case Flow and Nexus Reach on Sept. 29 for financial crime investigations. These offerings target compliance workloads where efficiency must coexist with accountability.

That same day, NetApp (NTAP) and Oracle announced OCI NetApp Storage Service, with general availability planned within 12 months. Its ONTAP capabilities would help customers migrate databases, enterprise applications, and AI workloads without substantially redesigning existing storage operations.

However, expansion brings obligations beyond hardware. On Oct. 2, Oracle committed to absorbing approximately $300 million in rising Point Beach nuclear energy costs, benefiting over 1 million Wisconsin utility customers. The company's related Project Lighthouse development projects more than $11 billion in local economic benefits, 4,000 construction jobs over three years, and 1,000 ongoing positions.

These initiatives give Oracle more ways to win cloud business, but they also add to the spending shareholders must weigh. The key is how quickly those commitments translate into revenue and stronger cash flow.

Wall Street's Case for Oracle

Oracle's next earnings report is scheduled for Dec. 9. Analysts expect November-quarter EPS of $1.57, down 19% from $1.95 a year earlier.

Despite that projected decline, Citi sees an opportunity. In August, the firm placed Oracle on a 90-day upside catalyst watch, maintaining a "Buy" rating and a $330 price target. Citi's thesis rests on AI infrastructure demand supporting stronger cloud growth, pricing, and profitability. Citi also identified earnings and an upcoming investor day as potential catalysts.

JPMorgan offered a more measured endorsement in August, retaining an "Overweight" rating while cutting its target to $200 from $210. Analyst Samik Chatterjee noted aggressive infrastructure spending and capital requirements but maintained that Oracle could capitalize on AI expansion.

That optimism extends beyond Citi and JPMorgan. Across 43 analysts with coverage, ORCL stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. The average price target of $242.22 implies potential upside of approximately 86% from current levels.

Conclusion

Oracle looks more like a cautious buy than a stock to avoid. Strong cloud growth supports the opportunity, but heavy spending and negative free cash flow warrant smaller positions rather than aggressive buying. A gradual recovery looks more likely than a quick rebound, provided demand holds and financing remains manageable. The next earnings report will need to show that expansion is producing better financial results. Buying shares gradually makes sense here, but chasing a bounce before cash flow improves would be premature.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Shot Higher Today
news.Content:
Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) charged sharply higher on Monday, jumping as much as 8.3%. As of 11:24 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 7.9%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

While a rebound in technology issues certainly helped, the semiconductor specialist rallied on positive news in the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) space.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Industry standard

Earlier this year, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced the development of NVHBM, the company's custom HBM architecture. NVHBM is a custom HBM die that delivers 15% lower power consumption and 30% higher bandwidth, all on a smaller die than HBM4e. To be clear, this isn't a replacement for traditional HBM, but rather connective technology between Nvidia's NVLink and HBM chips.

A report emerged over the weekend that Nvidia has asked Samsung Electronics to adopt Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing 's 3-nanometer chipmaking process to produce the NVHBM dies, according to a story that first appeared in the Seoul Economic Daily. This will mark the first such collaboration between TSMC and Samsung, according to the report.

Moreover, Nvidia has approached the industry's biggest memory producers, including Micron Technology and SK Hynix , to use this process, which would standardize it across multiple memory suppliers. This, in turn, would free up valuable real estate on the compute die, resulting in up to 30% additional compute.

Investors have been concerned that demand for artificial intelligence (AI) could falter, thereby reducing demand for the AI chips. This move by Nvidia suggests that -- despite fears to the contrary -- the adoption of AI still has room to run. This suggests that the same is true for memory chip suppliers.

Even in the face of unprecedented demand for memory chips, Sandisk stock is selling for just 19 times earnings and 6 times forward earnings. This gives investors the opportunity to pick up shares at a discount.

news.Title: If Apple Cuts iPhone Units in 2027, This Stock Could Be a Big Loser
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) is reportedly asking several key suppliers to scale back component production for its flagship devices, as higher retail prices driven by rising memory chip costs appear to be cooling consumer demand. And if iPhone sales lose steam, the ripple effects could reach far beyond Apple itself.

Take Cirrus Logic (CRUS), for instance. The semiconductor company relies heavily on Apple, which contributes the lion's share of its revenue, according to KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh. With Apple reportedly taking a more cautious approach to iPhone production, Vinh sees a risk that unit sales could stay flat or slip slightly in 2027, dampening Cirrus Logic's growth prospects. That concern prompted him to downgrade CRUS stock, adding to the pressure on shares.

More News from Barchart

Intel vs. AMD: The CPU Comeback Has Become a 2-Stock Fight, But 1 Is the Better Buy

Micron Stock Alert: Elon Musk Just Made The Bull Case Even Stronger

What a New Nvidia-Backed AI Platform Means for Honeywell Stock

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Cirrus supplies custom audio and mixed-signal chips used in smartphones, making it particularly sensitive to changes in Apple's production plans. With its potential PC growth opportunity also facing delays, investors have more than one reason to pay attention. So, if Apple trims iPhone production in 2027, could Cirrus Logic be among the biggest losers? Let's take a closer look.

About Cirrus Logic Stock

Founded in 1984, Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia. The company designs high-performance analog, mixed-signal, and audio digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits used in smartphones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches, automotive entertainment systems, and other consumer electronics.

Its product portfolio includes smart codecs, amplifiers, haptics and sensing solutions, camera controllers, and battery and power ICs. With approximately 1,717 employees worldwide, Cirrus Logic focuses on power efficiency, audio quality, and innovative chip designs. The company has a market capitalization of around $5.4 billion.

Cirrus Logic's stock started the year on a high note, climbing to $180.42 in May 2026 as strong fiscal 2026 results and optimism around the semiconductor sector gave investors plenty to cheer about. But that enthusiasm has since faded. By Oct. 15, shares had tumbled to a 52-week low of $105.10, down 40% from their peak. CRUS stock has lost 14% over the past year and 35% over six months, with recent losses reflecting softer PC market expectations and concerns about its heavy reliance on Apple, its largest customer.

Story Continues

Things got more interesting after Cirrus announced its acquisition of Italy-based INVENTVM Semiconductor on Oct. 6. The deal aims to expand its technology portfolio and reach new markets, but the financial terms remain undisclosed, and management expects no material revenue impact. That may explain why investors have not warmed up to the deal just yet, as they weigh its long-term potential against the lack of an immediate financial boost.

Technically, CRUS stock shows signs of stabilization, but the picture remains shaky. The 14-day RSI has bounced back from oversold territory to around 34, though it is still below the neutral mark. Meanwhile, the MACD line remains below its signal line, with a negative histogram pointing to continued bearish momentum.

On the valuation front, CRUS stock looks relatively affordable, trading at 12.88 times forward adjusted earnings and 2.68 times forward sales. Both multiples sit below the stock's five-year averages and those of its sector peers, making its current valuation worth a closer look.

A Closer Look at Cirrus Logic's Q1 Earnings Report

In August, Cirrus Logic released its Q1 2027 earnings report and started the year on a strong note, posting record first-quarter revenue and earnings. That's largely due to healthy demand for custom chips used in premium smartphones. The company also made progress on its broader growth plans, although its PC business faced a few speed bumps.

Revenue rose 12.9% year-over-year (YoY) to $460 million, almost in line with Wall Street's expectations. Sales also increased 2.5% sequentially as stronger shipments of smartphone components lifted results. Demand for custom-boosted amplifiers and smart codecs remained strong, helping the company deliver record quarterly earnings. Adjusted EPS climbed 21.9% annually to $1.84, beating analysts' estimates. However, previously anticipated pricing reductions partly offset the revenue gains. Cirrus remains heavily reliant on its biggest customer, Apple, which accounted for 90% of first-quarter revenue.

Beyond smartphones, Cirrus is working to expand its footprint in AI-enabled PCs and other markets. Interest in its latest low-power smart codec for AI PCs remains strong, with multiple customers working on designs expected to launch next calendar year. However, supply constraints involving a key industry platform, memory and other components, along with delayed PC launches, have pushed expected growth further out.

As a result, management lowered its fiscal 2027 PC revenue expectations, describing the challenges as timing issues rather than a change in the long-term opportunity. Several customers have also announced PCs based on Nvidia's (NVDA) RTX Spark platform that are expected to ship later this year with Cirrus amplifiers and codecs.

The company is also advancing its next-generation camera controller and smart power IC for 3D sensing, while a newly taped-out high-performance analog front-end component targeting metrology applications adds to its general market portfolio.

Cirrus ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and investments and no debt. Operating cash flow reached $64.1 million, while free cash flow came in at $48.6 million, representing an 11% margin. The company repurchased about 211,000 shares for $34.5 million during the quarter and bought another 359,000 shares for $50.5 million after quarter-end. Management continues to prioritize investments in the business, followed by acquisitions and share buybacks, with no near-term dividend planned.

Looking ahead, Cirrus expects Q2 revenue between $510 million and $570 million, with the midpoint implying 17% sequential growth but roughly 4% YoY decline. GAAP gross margin is projected at 52% to 54%. While smartphone demand remains a key support, investors will be watching whether Cirrus can turn its growing AI-PC pipeline into meaningful revenue as supply constraints ease.

Cirrus Logic is gearing up to report its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the closing bell, and Wall Street will be watching to see how the chipmaker is holding up. Analysts expect revenue to come in at around $540.4 million, while EPS is projected to slip nearly 16% YoY to $2.11. Looking further ahead, fiscal 2027 earnings are expected to fall 8.9% annually to $7.24 per share. There could be some relief in fiscal 2028, though, with EPS projected to rebound 4.7% YoY to $7.58.

What Do Analysts Think About CRUS Stock?

KeyBanc downgraded CRUS stock to a "Sector Weight" from an "Overweight," citing its heavy reliance on Apple and delayed diversification prospects. Analyst John Vinh noted that Apple's cuts to TSMC (TSM) wafer starts, equivalent to 15 million to 20 million iPhones, suggest weaker iPhone volumes in 2027.

With roughly 90% of Cirrus Logic's revenue tied to Apple, Vinh sees limited growth over the next six to 12 months. Meanwhile, elevated memory prices and an expected 10% to 15% decline in PC shipments this year could delay its PC diversification plans, despite meaningful share gains in the segment. KeyBanc also questioned Cirrus' unsuccessful Synaptics (SYNA) acquisition bid from a strategic standpoint.

Analysts have been moderately bullish about Cirrus Logic, with seven who cover the stock giving a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Among them, three suggest a "Strong Buy," three are playing it safe with a "Hold" rating, while the remaining one has a "Strong Sell."

The mean price target of $123.20 indicates CRUS has an upside potential of 13%, and the high target of $200 suggests that the stock could rise as much as 83% from the current price level.

news.Title: Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) Upgraded to Strong Buy: Here's What You Should Know
news.Content:
Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) could be a solid addition to your portfolio given its recent upgrade to a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). This upgrade primarily reflects an upward trend in earnings estimates, which is one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.

The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.

Individual investors often find it hard to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, since these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time. In these situations, the Zacks rating system comes in handy because of the power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements.

Therefore, the Zacks rating upgrade for Sandisk Corporation basically reflects positivity about its earnings outlook that could translate into buying pressure and an increase in its stock price.

Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices

The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated. The influence of institutional investors has a partial contribution to this relationship, as these big professionals use earnings and earnings estimates to calculate the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.

For Sandisk Corporation, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade fundamentally mean an improvement in the company's underlying business. And investors' appreciation of this improving business trend should push the stock higher.

Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions

As empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock movements, tracking such revisions for making an investment decision could be truly rewarding. Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.

The Zacks Rank stock-rating system, which uses four factors related to earnings estimates to classify stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), has an impressive externally-audited track record, with Zacks Rank #1 stocks generating an average annual return of +25% since 1988. Analysts have been steadily raising their estimates for Sandisk Corporation. Over the past three months, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company has increased 12.4%.

Bottom Line

Unlike the overly optimistic Wall Street analysts whose rating systems tend to be weighted toward favorable recommendations, the Zacks rating system maintains an equal proportion of "buy" and "sell" ratings for its entire universe of more than 4,000 stocks at any point in time. Irrespective of market conditions, only the top 5% of the Zacks-covered stocks get a "Strong Buy" rating and the next 15% get a "Buy" rating. So, the placement of a stock in the top 20% of the Zacks-covered stocks indicates its superior earnings estimate revision feature, making it a solid candidate for producing market-beating returns in the near term.

Based on current estimates, the P/E could decline to roughly 28x on 2028 earnings and 21x on 2029 earnings. This means much of the earnings investors are paying for today is expected to arrive within one to three years. The company's near sold-out capacity lends more support to those projections.

The stock is not undervalued, but its premium could be reasonable if Lumentum adds capacity as planned. Demand is already there; production capacity is now the key factor limiting growth.

news.Title: SanDisk Stock Is Caught in the China Chip Selloff. Here’s What Investors Are Missing.
news.Content:
China's latest memory-chip breakthrough has sent SanDisk (SNDK) stock into a tailspin. SNDK stock has surged 447% year-to-date (YTD), but the rally has stalled, with shares down 18% over the past five days as investors brace for tougher competition in the memory space. But the market may be overlooking an important distinction. Not all memory chips serve the same purpose. The new technology from China that is shaking up the market focuses on DRAM, but SanDisk mainly works with NAND flash storage.

That distinction could be getting lost in the selloff. Let's take a closer look.

More News from Barchart

Intel vs. AMD: The CPU Comeback Has Become a 2-Stock Fight, But 1 Is the Better Buy

Micron Stock Alert: Elon Musk Just Made The Bull Case Even Stronger

What a New Nvidia-Backed AI Platform Means for Honeywell Stock

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

China's Latest Memory Breakthrough Has Spooked Investors

Memory stocks faced new pressure after Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) recently announced it is working to increase the density of its DRAM products. The company has made progress on a new 4F² chip design and expects to bring its new server-focused DRAM technology to market before the end of 2026. This technology makes each memory cell smaller, so manufacturers can fit more memory into the same amount of space.

This news has renewed worries about China's potential to compete with established memory manufacturers. SanDisk shares fell alongside other memory and semiconductor stocks like Micron (MU), Samsung, and SK Hynix (SKHY) as investors reassessed the competition and questioned how long the artificial intelligence (AI) investment surge might last.

SanDisk Makes NAND, Not DRAM

If CXMT eventually produces competitive chips at scale, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix face a direct competitive threat from the DRAM breakthrough. SanDisk, however, may be less affected because its main business is NAND flash storage.

DRAM gives processors fast, temporary working memory that computers and servers use while running applications. NAND, on the other hand, keeps data even when the power is off and is widely used in solid-state drives and other storage devices. Both are important for present-day computing, but they have different uses and cannot always replace each other. This means CXMT's new DRAM architecture does not directly replace the NAND products that SanDisk currently sells. So, even if the selloff makes it seem that way, it does not have direct competitive consequences for SanDisk.

Story Continues

CXMT's plans could intensify DRAM competition, especially if it delivers strong server-memory products at scale. Still, announcing new technology is not the same as proving a product can be made reliably, sold at a good price, and attract customers from established suppliers.

SanDisk's Numbers Show Why Bulls Aren't Giving Up

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, SanDisk reported revenue of $8.97 billion, up 51% from the prior quarter and 372% year-over-year (YOY). Management said this strong result came from increased sales and better prices, thanks to a healthy market for NAND products.

Data-center demand played a key role. SanDisk reported $2.98 billion in data-center revenue for the quarter, up 103% sequentially. For fiscal 2026, revenue stood at $20.25 billion, a 175% YOY increase driven by data-center revenue growth of 437%. These numbers highlight how quickly the company has gained from the rising need for storage infrastructure.

SanDisk's profits grew even more during the quarter. Adjusted gross margin was 84.6% in Q4, while adjusted diluted EPS jumped to $39.25 from $0.29 a year earlier. Management explained that higher prices accounted for about two-thirds of the quarter's revenue growth, while increased sales volume accounted for the rest. This combination shows that the company is benefiting from both higher demand and better pricing.

Management believes that growing AI infrastructure will increase demand for NAND. As more AI models run inference, data centers are required to store and access more data. Enterprise SSDs are important here, especially when capacity, power use, and data access are key. This gives SanDisk a chance to expand beyond just consumer storage devices. SanDisk expects strong demand and profitability to continue into Q1 fiscal 2027. The company expects Q1 revenue between $10.3 billion and $10.8 billion, adjusted gross margin of about 83% to 85%, and adjusted diluted EPS ranging from $44 to $46.

Although CXMT's latest development is focused on DRAM, the wider effects of China's growing semiconductor industry are still something to watch. Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), another Chinese company, makes NAND flash memory. That means its progress likely matters more to SanDisk, since both companies compete in the NAND market.

What the China Chip News Means for SNDK Stock

SanDisk's recent drop may not only be about concerns over China. It could also reflect worries about more competition in the memory market, questions about AI spending, and some investors cashing in after a big rally. While China's memory progress is worth watching, SanDisk's NAND business is holding its ground. The company's long-term outlook will depend on how well its storage products compete and whether growing demand for AI infrastructure drives steady earnings growth. Analysts project earnings to climb 201% in fiscal 2027, followed by 21% growth in fiscal 2028.

On Wall Street, SNDK stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating overall. Of the 25 analysts covering the stock, 21 recommend a "Strong Buy," one analyst has a "Moderate Buy," and three suggest a "Hold" rating. The average price target of $2,154.17 suggests potential upside of around 66% from current levels, while the Street-high estimate of $3,000 indicates SNDK stock could gain as much as 131% this year.

news.Title: Arm vs. Lumentum: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As artificial intelligence (AI) pushes computing power and data transmission to new limits, investors are weighing different paths to growth. Is Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) or Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) the better choice today?

Arm creates the foundational blueprints for the world's most energy-efficient processors. Lumentum provides the optical components that allow data centers to communicate at lightning speeds. Both companies are central to the infrastructure of modern computing, but they operate with vastly different business models and financial profiles.

The case for Arm

Arm designs and licenses central processing units (CPUs) and other systems used in everything from smartphones to high-performance data centers. Rather than manufacturing chips, the company earns revenue through licensing fees and royalties on every chip sold. This model enables high scalability and profit margins in the semiconductor industry .

In fiscal 2026 (ending in March), Arm's revenue reached $4.9 billion. This represents growth of nearly 23% compared to the prior year. Net income was roughly $698 million, though the net margin decreased slightly from roughly 16% in the previous year to about 14%.

As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, indicating the company has very little debt relative to its net equity. The current ratio is roughly 5.3x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations.

Trailing-12-month (TTM) free cash flow was $1.5 billion through the June quarter, but note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 69% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Lumentum

Lumentum manufactures optical and photonic products essential to cloud data centers and telecommunications networks. In its latest fiscal year ended June 27, 2026, Lumentum revealed that Customer A accounted for approximately 26.6% of revenue while Customer B accounted for roughly 15%. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as the loss of either client would be significant.

For fiscal 2026, the company reported revenue of $3 billion, which was an increase of about 83% over the prior year. Despite this massive top-line growth, the company reported a net loss of approximately $6.9 billion, although its operating profit (earnings before interest and taxes) was $525 million. The $6.9 billion net loss was due to a $7.7 billion non-recurring loss on debt extinguishment.

Story Continues

According to its June 2026 balance sheet, the company has a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x. The current ratio is nearly 1.7x, indicating about $1.70 in short-term assets for every $1.00 of short-term debt.

TTM free cash flow for the period was roughly $300 million. However, stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces intense competition from established rivals and open-source alternatives. If major tech companies decide to design their own architectures rather than paying licensing fees, the company could see its market share erode. Additionally, the business relies on continued growth in the mobile and data center markets, and any slowdown in hardware upgrades would impact its royalty income.

Lumentum is highly dependent on a small number of customers for a significant portion of its sales, and many relationships lack long-term volume commitments. The company is also subject to complex trade policies and export controls, specifically regarding operations in China. Competition from global firms such as IPG Photonics and Viavi Solutions exerts constant pressure on pricing and operating margins.

Valuation comparison

Lumentum appears to be the more value-oriented choice as it trades at a significant discount to its peer across both sales and future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Arm is a great business that generates high margins from royalties and licensing fees. It would be a solid chip stock to own, but Lumentum offers better value right now.

Analysts expect Arm to grow earnings at a 25% annualized rate in the coming years. However, Lumentum is expected to deliver 132% annualized growth, as the business scales and expands margins. Relative to their forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, Arm looks expensive, trading at a forward P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 4.3x, while Lumentum trades at an attractive 0.29x.

Lumentum is benefiting from data centers shifting to optical connectivity for AI workloads. Revenue surged 109% year over year in the recent quarter, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of growth and signaling strong momentum that may not be fully reflected in the stock's valuation right now.

Arm is benefiting from the growing demand for CPUs, and its expertise in designing power-efficient chips could help it gain market share in the data center market.

Both companies are meeting demand at crucial chokepoints for AI, and they both face comparable risks. But it's difficult for me to pass up the huge discrepancy between each stock's PEG ratios. I would buy Lumentum since it's growing much faster than Arm and commands a much lower premium for future earnings growth.

news.Title: Down 27.5% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) Looks Ripe for a Turnaround
news.Content:
Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) has been on a downward spiral lately with significant selling pressure. After declining 27.5% over the past four weeks, the stock looks well positioned for a trend reversal as it is now in oversold territory and there is strong agreement among Wall Street analysts that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Why a Trend Reversal is Due for SNDK

The RSI reading of 29.31 for SNDK is an indication that the heavy selling could be in the process of exhausting itself, so the stock could bounce back in a quest for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

This technical indicator is not the only factor that calls for a potential rebound for the stock. There is a fundamental indicator as well. A strong agreement among sell-side analysts covering SNDK in raising earnings estimates for the current year has led to an increase in the consensus EPS estimate by 0% over the last 30 days. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Moreover, SNDK currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. This is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential turnaround in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Factors Likely to Influence LRCX's Q1 Results

Lam Research's first-quarter performance is likely to have benefited from the surging demand for memory and advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. The rise in spending on AI and machine learning, particularly with the growing influence of Generative AI, is likely to have provided a significant boost to the company's performance in the fiscal first quarter. The increasing need for advanced AI-centric chips has become a key growth catalyst.

Heightened DRAM spending, especially in response to demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), is likely to have played in Lam Research's favor. The company's momentum in 3D DRAM and advanced packaging technologies is also expected to have added to its strong performance. At the same time, ongoing technological advancements are pushing NAND spending higher, which is likely to contribute to LRCX's quarterly results.

Story Continues

Lam Research's focus on expanding semiconductor fabrication capabilities, along with its heavy investment in research and development, positions it well in a competitive landscape. Its innovation through Semiverse solutions, particularly in high-aspect-ratio memory hole etch for NAND, is likely to have fueled this progress. LRCX's strategic investments in cutting-edge technologies are anticipated to have bolstered its performance in the foundry and logic segment, while the increasing adoption of 3D architectures is expected to have supported growth in its etch and deposition services.

The company's robust suite of tools, which enable foundry logic inflections, is likely to have secured strong customer traction. With the accelerating deployment of 5G and the Internet of Things (IoT), Lam Research's semiconductor and memory solutions remain in high demand, reinforcing its market position in the fiscal first quarter.

All these factors are likely to have driven growth in system revenues. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for first-quarter systems revenues is pegged at $5.61 billion, implying year-over-year growth of 58.2%, underscoring Lam Research's continued strength in the evolving tech landscape. The consensus mark for the Customer Support segment's first-quarter revenues is pegged at $2.50 billion, indicating a year-over-year increase of 40.6%.

LRCX's Stock Price Performance & Valuation

Lam Research shares have surged 54.2% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Electronics – Semiconductors industry, which has risen 12.6%. Compared with peers, the stock has outpaced ASML Holding ASML and KLA Corporation KLAC but underperformed Applied Materials AMAT. Shares of ASML Holding, KLAC and Applied Materials have soared 53.4%, 36.4% and 59.2%, respectively.

Lam Research YTD Price Return Performance

Let us look at the value Lam Research offers investors at current levels. Currently, LRCX is trading at a premium, with a forward 12-month P/E of 26.46X compared with the industry's 11.36X.

Lam Research Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Compared with semiconductor giants, the stock trades at a higher multiple than Applied Materials but at a lower multiple than KLA Corporation and ASML Holding. At present, Applied Materials, KLA Corp. and ASML Holding have forward 12-month P/E of 22.63X, 28.58X and 28.89X, respectively.

Investment Thesis on LRCX Stock

Lam Research is well-positioned to benefit from the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. The company provides advanced etch and deposition equipment used by leading chipmakers, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung.

As AI processors become more powerful, semiconductor manufacturers need more advanced processes, complex chip designs, advanced packaging and HBM. These trends increase the need for the type of equipment Lam Research provides.

The company's technology investments add to the growth opportunity. Its ALTUS ALD platform is aimed at improving manufacturing efficiency through molybdenum-based deposition, while the Aether platform supports the production of smaller and denser semiconductor structures.

Advanced packaging is another promising area. Lam Research expects revenues from this market to grow more than 70% in 2026 following strong growth in 2025. Emerging technologies such as backside power distribution and dry-resist processing could provide additional opportunities as semiconductor designs become increasingly complex.

Lam Research's consistent revenue growth is also encouraging. The company has generated more than $5 billion in quarterly revenues for five consecutive quarters, culminating in a record $6.72 billion in the last reported quarter. This consistency suggests the growth story is being supported by real semiconductor spending rather than just AI-related enthusiasm.

Final Verdict: Buy LRCX Stock for Now

Lam Research remains a high-quality AI infrastructure play with strong growth prospects. The AI infrastructure buildout remains in its early stages, advanced packaging demand continues to grow, and LRCX's leadership in etch and deposition gives it a competitive advantage that should be difficult to replicate.

Lam Research's innovation and operational efficiency provide a solid foundation for future growth. Considering these factors, accumulating LRCX stock appears to be the most prudent strategy for investors.

news.Title: Sandisk and Camping World have been highlighted as Zacks Bull and Bear of the Day
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 19, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Sandisk SNDK as the Bull of the Day and Camping World CWH as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on Tesla TSLA and SpaceX SPCX.

Here is a synopsis of all four stocks:

Bull of the Day:

There's an old saying on Wall Street that the trend is your friend. Well, when it comes to the technology sector, there are few trends more powerful than the artificial intelligence boom. We've seen the incredible run in NVIDIA and the companies building out AI infrastructure. But there's another corner of the market that has been absolutely on fire. I'm talking about memory and storage.

AI needs more than just powerful processors. It needs massive amounts of data, and that data needs somewhere to live. That's creating a tremendous opportunity for companies providing the infrastructure behind the AI revolution. One of those companies is today's Bull of the Day, Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) Sandisk .

Sandisk develops and manufactures NAND flash-based storage products, including solid-state drives, embedded storage solutions, and consumer memory products. The company returned to the public markets as a standalone business in February 2025 following its separation from Western Digital. Since then, investors have been treated to an incredible rally as demand for high-performance storage has exploded.

Sandisk is in the Computer – Storage Devices industry, which ranks in the Top 10% of our Zacks Industry Rank. That's a very favorable backdrop for a stock already benefiting from some of the strongest growth trends in technology.

Sandisk Corporation Price and Consensus

The numbers behind this company are nothing short of staggering. Sandisk recently reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $39.25 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 14.63%. Revenue surged 371.6% year over year to $8.97 billion, exceeding expectations by roughly 8%. Datacenter revenue jumped 103% sequentially to $2.98 billion as hyperscalers continued gobbling up storage capacity to support AI workloads.

That growth is translating into incredible profitability. Non-GAAP gross margins expanded to 84.6%, up from 78.4% in the previous quarter. Think about that for a second. This is a company selling storage products, yet it's generating margins that would make plenty of software companies jealous.

Revenue estimates tell a similar story. Analysts are looking for fiscal 2027 sales of $49.25 billion, up from $20.25 billion in fiscal 2026. That's more than 143% revenue growth. Fiscal 2028 sales are projected to climb another 19% to $58.46 billion.

Story Continues

The reason for the favorable rank is that over the last sixty days, analysts have upped the ante for both the current year and next year. The bullish moves have pushed up our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year from $192.82 to $213.31 and next year up from $181.88 to $252.80. The stock has had some pressure recently because of the financing questions popping up in the Neocloud space. This should eventually work itself out. While investors know the numbers can't grow like this forever, they should be enjoying the profits while they can.

Bear of the Day:

The stock market can be a cruel place sometimes. Just when you think things can't get any worse, the selling continues. That's especially true for companies that are struggling to find their footing in an economy where consumers are becoming increasingly selective about how they spend their money. Big-ticket discretionary purchases are particularly vulnerable. When financing costs are high and consumers are feeling the pinch, buying a new recreational vehicle isn't exactly at the top of everyone's priority list.

That's creating some serious headaches for today's Bear of the Day, Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) Camping World . Camping World Holdings is one of the nation's largest retailers of recreational vehicles. The company operates a network of RV dealerships, offering new and used motorhomes, travel trailers, and fifth wheels. It also provides financing, insurance, service, maintenance, and accessories through its Camping World and Good Sam brands.

It's a business that benefited tremendously from the pandemic-era boom in outdoor recreation. Consumers had money to spend, financing was cheap, and RV sales were booming. Unfortunately, that environment has changed considerably. Higher borrowing costs, affordability pressures, and a more cautious consumer have created a much more challenging backdrop for the RV industry.

That weakness is showing up where it matters most to us here at Zacks. I'm talking about earnings estimates. Over the last thirty days, four analysts have lowered their earnings estimates for the current year. Not a single analyst has increased estimates during that period. The bearish sentiment has pushed the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year down from 36 cents to just 20 cents per share. That's a decline of nearly 44% in only two months.

Next year's numbers aren't looking much better. Four analysts have also cut their estimates for the following year, pushing the consensus down from 87 cents to 56 cents per share. That's a reduction of more than 35%. Those downward revisions are the primary reason Camping World currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

Camping World Price and Consensus

The industry backdrop isn't doing the company any favors either. Camping World is part of the Automotive – Original Equipment industry, which ranks in the Bottom 13% of our Zacks Industry Rank. That's not exactly the sort of neighborhood I want to be shopping in when the broader market is already dealing with uncertainty.

Additional content:

Roadster Hype Can't Mask Tesla's Margin & FCF Woes Before Q3 Earnings

Tesla and its CEO Elon Musk know how to command a stage. Yesterday's Roadster event featured rocket-assisted flips, a car launching off a ramp, and Musk declaring that the future includes flying cars. But the stock's real test is the earnings report on Oct. 21, and no stunt can change the mood heading into the release.

Impressive and a Bit Gimmicky, Roadster Is Years Away

The demo was designed to dazzle and Tesla's loyal fans were certain to lap it up. The Roadster climbed a giant curved ramp, clung to it with a fan-based suction system until it was upside down, then used cold-gas thrusters developed with SpaceX to launch, flip in midair and land cleanly. In a second stunt, it vaulted over a row of cars and a semi-truck. The Roadster was shown hitting 60 mph in under a second, though the 230-mph top speed is Musk's claim for certain versions.

Tesla is already taking money. A "Performance" reservation needs a $50,000 deposit, the "Thrust" version with acceleration thrusters needs $250,000, and an invite-only single-seat "Rocket" variant promises a full flight system.

Yet production isn't expected until 2028, nearly a decade after the car was first unveiled in 2017. For a company under margin and free cash flow pressure and pivoting toward robotics and self-driving, we might as well dismiss the Roadster demo as engineering showmanship that adds little to the business.

TSLA's Reality: Deliveries Held Up, Profits Not Likely To

Tesla's third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 471,262 and marked Tesla's best quarter in a year. Deliveries were still 2.1% below the same quarter last year, but that was a period inflated by Americans rushing to buy before federal EV tax credits expired.

The concern is that the volume isn't turning into profit. In the second quarter of 2026, automotive gross margin (excluding regulatory credits) slid to 16.3% amid persistent price cuts. The energy storage business, once a bright spot, saw margins collapse from 39.5% to 20.4%. Selling more while earning less on each sale is worrying for investors.

The Rising Bill for TSLA's Future Bets

Meanwhile, spending is climbing. Capital expenditure is expected to exceed $25 billion in 2026. Second-quarter 2026 FCF turned negative to $1.09 billion, and the metric will be under pressure in the near term.

Capex is going into autonomy, AI, robotics and manufacturing capacity. Optimus is still early-stage, and Cybercab is only starting to scale. Both may pay off someday, but for now they are expenses, and Tesla hasn't offered a clear timeline for when they will produce meaningful returns.

The Valuation Gap We Can't Ignore

The share price assumes autonomy and robotics will become major profit engines. The businesses funding those bets, cars and energy storage, are earning less. The distance between what investors expect and what Tesla is currently delivering is the biggest risk, and a rich valuation leaves little room to defend it. Tesla carries a Value Score of F. Analysts appear to sense this, with earnings estimates being trimmed ahead of the report.

The Bottom Line

The Roadster might be creating buzz, but a flying demo can't repair shrinking margins, and a 2028 launch date can't pay this year's bills. Musk may be excited, and so may Tesla's faithful, but earnings are where the numbers get tested.

With margins sliding, spending rising and estimates falling, the risk heading into third-quarter results looks tilted to the downside.

The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

news.Title: U.S. Stock Futures Climb as Chipmakers Rebound; Corporate Earnings in Focus
news.Content:
December S&P 500 E-Mini futures (ESZ26) are up +0.52%, and December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are up +1.11% this morning as investors cautiously snapped up beaten-down chipmakers and other AI-related stocks, setting a positive tone for a busy week of corporate earnings.

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks climbed in pre-market trading, rebounding from last week's rout. Intel (INTC) was up over +4%, Marvell Technology (MRVL) was up more than +3%, and Micron Technology (MU) was up over +2%.

More News from Barchart

What a New Nvidia-Backed AI Platform Means for Honeywell Stock

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The price of WTI crude edged lower on Monday as traders weighed Washington's decision to lift newly imposed sanctions on Russia against lingering Middle East supply risks. U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving sanctions and tariffs imposed under a new law targeting Russia, potentially paving the way for more Russian diesel exports to reach international markets. Still, ongoing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and elevated shipping costs limited oil's losses.

Treasuries were mixed, with shorter-dated bonds edging lower and longer-dated bonds posting modest gains.

In Friday's trading session, Wall Street's major equity averages closed sharply lower, weighed down by a surge in oil prices and concerns about the viability of the AI trade. Chip and AI infrastructure stocks sank, with Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) slumping over -7% and Arm Holdings (ARM) dropping more than -6%. Also, most members of the Magnificent Seven slid, with Meta Platforms (META) falling over -3% and Alphabet (GOOGL) slipping more than -2% to lead losers in the Dow. In addition, CoreWeave (CRWV) tumbled more than -11% amid lingering concerns about the cloud-computing company's ability to repay its debt. On the bullish side, energy stocks advanced as oil prices surged, with Diamondback Energy (FANG) climbing over +4% to lead gainers in the Nasdaq 100 and APA Corp. (APA) rising more than +4%.

Economic data released on Friday were mixed for equities. U.S. industrial production rose +0.7% m/m in September, stronger than expectations of +0.4% m/m, and manufacturing production rose +0.3% m/m, in line with expectations. At the same time, the U.S. import price index climbed +1.1% m/m in September, exceeding expectations of +0.9% m/m and marking its second straight monthly increase.

Story Continues

"Too many traders piled into the AI trade, with the bullseye now squarely on worries surrounding funding issues. CoreWeave's issues put even more pressure on Big Tech and AI companies to deliver strong earnings results in the coming weeks," said Dan Eye at Focus Partners Wealth.

Third-quarter corporate earnings season gathers momentum this week, with Big Tech in the spotlight. Investors will closely watch earnings from Magnificent Seven stalwarts Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA). Meta's results will draw particular attention, as the company will be the first hyperscaler to report following the rout in chip stocks and growing concerns that rising credit costs could derail the AI boom. Beyond the Mag Seven heavyweights, major companies including SpaceX (SPCX), Lam Research (LRCX), Texas Instruments (TXN), International Business Machines (IBM), Western Digital (WDC), Netflix (NFLX), GE Aerospace (GE), RTX Corp. (RTX), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Philip Morris International (PM), Procter & Gamble (PG), and American Express Company (AXP) are set to report quarterly results this week. According to Bloomberg Intelligence, S&P 500 companies are expected to post an average +25% jump in third-quarter earnings from a year earlier.

The busy earnings calendar is balanced out by a relatively light economic data slate. Preliminary U.S. October purchasing managers' surveys for manufacturing and services will be the main highlight this week, offering insight into how the economy has fared this month. Other noteworthy data releases include building permits (preliminary), housing starts, pending home sales, initial jobless claims, the Conference Board Leading Economic Index, and the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index.

U.S. central bankers are in a media blackout period before the October 27-28 policy meeting. During that period, policymakers do not speak publicly about the economic outlook or monetary policy.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in an 85.1% chance of no rate change and a 14.9% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the October FOMC meeting.

Elsewhere, Nvidia (NVDA) will host its GTC Berlin AI conference this week, with CEO Jensen Huang set to deliver a speech.

The U.S. economic data slate is largely empty on Monday.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 5.08%, down -0.18%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -0.96% this morning, kicking off the new week on a downbeat note after a weekend of violent protests in France. The unrest extended to major cities in Belgium, Italy, and Portugal, sapping investors' risk appetite. Bank stocks led the declines on Monday. Travel and defense stocks also slumped. French government bond yields surged on Monday, widening the spread with German yields as the protests fueled concerns about political instability ahead of next year's French presidential election, adding to existing worries about debt. This week, investors will closely watch the preliminary Eurozone PMIs for October. "Given the upturn in sentiment over the past few months, we expect a slight pullback [in the PMIs]. Taken on its own, this could push the recent bond-positive trends a bit further," according to LBBW analysts. Germany's ZEW economic sentiment index for October and the European Central Bank's consumer expectations survey will also draw attention. In addition, several ECB officials are scheduled to speak this week, including President Christine Lagarde and Chief Economist Philip Lane. In corporate news, Mowi ASA (MOWI.O.DX) climbed more than +4% after the salmon producer reported record harvest volumes for the third quarter.

The European economic data slate is empty on Monday.

Asian stock markets today settled mixed. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed up +0.39%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -0.62%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed higher today after data showed that the country's economy grew more than expected in the third quarter. Traditional sectors, including banking and liquor, led the gains on Monday. At the same time, technology stocks slumped as sentiment toward the AI chip supply chain remained weak. Data from the National Bureau of Statistics released on Monday showed that China's economic growth accelerated in the third quarter, rebounding from a three-year low as surging exports helped offset a deepening domestic slowdown. China's GDP expanded 4.5% in the third quarter, bringing growth in the first nine months of the year to 4.6%—within the government's annual target range of 4.5%-5%. Separate data showed that growth in industrial production and retail sales, a key gauge of domestic consumption, picked up in September, although the latter lagged well behind the former. In addition, data showed that declines in China's home prices moderated slightly last month, likely supported by Beijing's measures to revive the struggling property sector, including subsidies for mortgage borrowers. "The September data do suggest that the economy regained momentum at the end of the third quarter and we expect a further acceleration over the coming months as increased fiscal support kicks in," according to Capital Economics analysts. Investor attention now turns to the People's Bank of China, which is set to announce the country's benchmark lending rates on Tuesday. Economists expect the one-year loan prime rate to stay unchanged at 3.00% and the five-year LPR at 3.50% after better-than-expected GDP data reduced the likelihood of near-term monetary easing.

The Chinese GDP rose +1.2% q/q and +4.5% y/y in the third quarter, stronger than expectations of +1.1% q/q and +4.4% y/y.

The Chinese September Industrial Production rose +5.5% y/y, stronger than expectations of +5.4% y/y.

The Chinese September Retail Sales rose +1.1% y/y, stronger than expectations of +0.5% y/y.

The Chinese Fixed Asset Investment fell -7.2% y/y in the January-September period, stronger than expectations of -7.3% y/y.

The Chinese September Unemployment Rate was 5.2%, stronger than expectations of no change at 5.3%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed lower today, although it pared most of its earlier losses as the rebound in U.S. stock index futures offered some relief to investors. The Nikkei initially plunged as much as 2.3% as chip-related stocks tracked Friday's selloff in their U.S. peers. However, the benchmark recouped most of its losses in the afternoon session as chip-related shares trimmed their earlier declines following the surge in Nasdaq 100 futures. Gains in energy and industrial stocks also supported the index. Meanwhile, Japanese government bond yields fell on Monday as some investors sought refuge in safe-haven assets amid volatility surrounding the AI trade. Bonds also drew support from Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who said Japan would "appropriately" control the size of its debt issuance. Elsewhere, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Monday that underlying inflation is "quite close" to the central bank's 2% target, with robust global AI demand compounding price pressures from a tight labor market, signaling scope for further interest-rate hikes. In corporate news, Suzuken Co. rose over +2% after Nomura upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral with a price target of 3,550 yen. Investor focus this week is on Japan's national core CPI for September, which will provide further insight into whether inflationary pressures remain sufficiently strong to support the Bank of Japan's monetary policy normalization path. Market participants will also closely watch Japan's preliminary October PMIs and September trade figures. In addition, the BOJ will publish its semiannual Financial System Report at the end of the week. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed down -2.92% at 31.23.

Pre-Market U.S. Stock Movers

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks climbed in pre-market trading. Intel (INTC) was up over +4%, Marvell Technology (MRVL) was up more than +3%, and Micron Technology (MU) was up over +2%.

Most members of the Magnificent Seven edged higher in pre-market trading, with Nvidia (NVDA) and Amazon.com (AMZN) gaining more than +1%.

Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) jumped over +13% in pre-market trading after the steelmaker swung to a profit in Q3 and projected adjusted EBITDA exceeding $4 billion in 2027.

Datadog (DDOG) rose over +3% in pre-market trading after Bernstein upgraded the stock to Outperform from Market Perform with a price target of $350.

Ameriprise Financial (AMP) fell more than -1% in pre-market trading after BofA double-downgraded the stock to Underperform from Buy with a price target of $445.

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉 中國Q3經濟成長反彈至4.5% 三大指數漲跌互見
news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周一（19日）收盤漲跌互見，中國第三季經濟成長加速，且優於經濟學家預期，提升了達成北京當局全年目標的機率，也降低了政府推出額外寬鬆措施的可能性。

上證指數周一收報3,730.92點，漲0.39%。深證成指收報11,817.42點，漲0.13%。創業板指收報2,746.29點，跌0.94%。

根據中國國家統計局周一公布的數據，第三季國內生產毛額（GDP）年增4.5%，增幅大於第二季的4.3%，亦優於經濟學家預測的4.4%。

這使得今年前九個月的經濟擴張幅度達到4.6%，落在政府設定的4.5%至5%全年目標區間。

經濟的反彈應能給政策制定者一些喘息空間，使政府官員得以暫緩推出更多寬鬆措施，目前政府官員仍受到銀行利差收窄以及地方政府持續面臨財政壓力的限制。

此外，9月工業生產年增率加速至 5.5%，符合經濟學家預期。零售銷售反彈幅度遠超預估，來到 1.1%，8月僅成長0.4%。

今年前九個月固定資產投資縮減7.2%，降幅與前八個月相同。

儘管近幾個月中國經濟放緩加劇，政府官員最初仍聚焦於落實既有促成長政策，直到三周前才加大支持力道，推出一項新的定向措施。

這個世界第二大經濟體的成長呈現兩極化：一方面是受到全球人工智慧（AI）投資超級周期的帶動，出口表現極為強勁；另一方面則是家庭支出疲軟，投資亦長期欲振乏力。

此外，就業市場降溫，長達數年的房市低迷也在持續拖累國內經濟。

疲弱內需使中國的經濟成長日益依賴出口。這讓北京面臨的貿易夥伴壓力越來越大，貿易夥伴要求中方解決龐大貿易順差問題——今年這項數字預計將打破2025年創下的 1.2 兆美元紀錄。

歐盟正準備賦予自身新權限，可能允許其封鎖中國進入歐盟單一市場的管道，作為雙邊貿易重新平衡的一環。

與此同時，外國領袖已呼籲北京當局允許人民幣更大幅度的升值，指出人民幣被低估，給予中國出口商不公平競爭優勢。

news.Title: 空軍轟炸台股！重災區「6檔記憶體」崩跌逾5%
news.Content: 財經中心／李明融報導 美股費城半導體指數重挫3.83%、狂吞罕見「連8黑」，引爆台股週一補跌震撼！台北股市今（19）日開盤空軍無情轟炸，加權指數早盤一度暴跌逾860點，最低摜至46,243.55點，電子權值股與半導體供應鏈全線跳水。其中，記憶體概念股更淪為大盤重災區，包括南亞科、華邦電、旺宏等指標大廠全面遭遇外資狂抽銀根，盤中高達6檔記憶體個股慘摔超過5%以上，族群呈現一片慘綠，市場避險與恐慌情緒急遽升溫。 記憶體族群慘遭血洗，威剛、南亞科重摔逾6%。（圖／民視新聞資料照） 記憶體族群慘遭血洗！威剛、南亞科重摔逾6%「6檔指標股」暴跌逾5% 觀察盤面個股表現，記憶體族群賣壓最為沉重，多檔個股同步跳空急殺。盤中跌幅超過5%的重災區名單多達6檔，其中以模組大廠威剛（3260）重摔6.67%、下跌24元至336元最為劇烈；記憶體大廠南亞科（2408）重挫6.15%、大跌27.5元來到420元；旺宏（2337）與華邦電（2344）跌幅分別達6.07%及5.88%，力積電（6770）與晶豪科（3006）跌幅也全數突破5.5%。此外，群聯重挫逾4%、力成、創見、廣穎及十銓等供應鏈個股同樣難逃波及，跌幅均在3%至4%之間，僅商丞力守平盤，整體記憶體概念股幾乎全軍覆沒。 權王台積電失守，中小型櫃買指數挫逾3%。（圖／民視新聞資料照） 美股費半連8黑拖累大盤！權王台積電失守中小型櫃買指數挫逾3% 台股早盤的崩跌走勢，主要反映美股上週五科技股疲弱引發的全球連鎖效應，道瓊、標普、那斯達克全面收黑，費半重挫更直接拖累台積電ADR下跌2.28%，讓台股面臨巨大補跌壓力。權值股方面，台積電（2330）早盤最低下探2,390元、下跌30元（跌幅1.24%），聯電重挫超過4%，鴻海也下挫1.84%；代表中小型股的櫃買指數（OTC）更是重摔逾3%，半導體類股指數下跌1.82%，顯示空方全面肆虐，大盤後續能否藉由低檔買盤收斂跌幅並守住支撐，仍端看美股科技股與權值龍頭能否盡快止跌回穩。 《民視新聞網》提醒您：內容僅供參考，投資人於決策時應審慎評估風險，並就投資結果自行負責。

news.Title: What Do the 8% of Analysts Who Will Not Buy Marvell (MRVL) See?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL ) closed at $241.24 on October 15. The stock has returned 80.88% over the last six months, compared to a 15.4% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 11.4% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

Marvell designs custom chips for the companies running large data centres. When a cloud provider wants its own processor rather than a standard one, Marvell is among the small group of firms that can design it. As per CNN, of the analysts covering the stock, 92% rate it a buy. The other 8% do not, and since the bull case has been made everywhere, the more interesting question is what the holdouts see.

READ ALSO: 10 Best Fundamental Stocks to Invest in According to Billionaires

The Case Almost Everyone Agrees With:

The growth is not in doubt. Revenue rose 36.5% in the most recent quarter, and the shares are up 174% over twelve months.

The work itself is sticky. A customer that commits to a custom design cannot switch supplier without starting the engineering again, which takes years. That buys Marvell a position no standard chip vendor gets.

Marvell appears in our 10 Most Promising Technology Stocks to Buy Right Now , alongside several names analysts see even further to run. To see them, click HERE .

DON'T MISS: 12 Most Profitable American Stocks to Buy in 2026

What the Minority Is Weighing:

The first thing is the price. Marvell trades at 62.11 times what analysts expect next year, which is by some distance the most demanding multiple on our list of ten.

The second is profitability. Operating margin runs at 16.68%. That is respectable for most industries and modest next to the other companies selling into artificial intelligence, several of which earn three or four times as much on every dollar of sales.

The third is who the customers are. Custom silicon work comes from a handful of very large technology firms, and the stickiness that protects Marvell also means a lost design is lost for the life of the product. The same feature that reads as a moat is the thing that makes each decision matter so much.

What the Gap Is Really Measuring:

The holdouts are not arguing that the business is in trouble. They are arguing about what it is worth.

That is the honest shape of the disagreement here. Nobody doubts the growth or the position. The question is whether a company earning these margins should carry a multiple several times what its larger and more profitable peers do.

Conclusion:

The minority view is not a bear case about the business. It is a bear case about the price, which is a different thing and easier to be right about. Marvell is winning work that is hard to take away and growing quickly on the back of it. The margins it earns are ordinary by the standards of its own industry, and the multiple is not. Decide which of those two facts you are buying, because the multiple assumes only one of them matters.
